# Address and Brief Introduction.

<margin>1.</margin><image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop-cap initial 'E' featuring intricate scrollwork and foliage patterns.</image-desc>It can and must / impartial and truth-seeking reader / every general good gift and seed from the Father of Lights <note>A biblical reference to James 1:17: "Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights."</note> / not otherwise / than through His communication and outflow / become and remain general and fruitful / if it / by virtue of the All-wise Divine Order / is to reach its final cause / and in infinite multiplication / become recognizable and stirring within us / namely, that it has its origin and essence / out of eternity and from GOD; Also for that reason / through yearning desire / to move and work / to lead its entire capacity and life / back again into its first source-fountain and wellspring / and to bring it into rest / it labors to the utmost / as we can daily experience and learn this from the essential-point of all created creatures / according to the distinction of their kind and seed; So that one learns to clearly recognize and distinguish the seed from the fruit / and from this / the tree and the fruit / according to their natural kind.

<margin>2.</margin>Hereby we observe / the very greatest power / and high-mighty glory / together with the unsearchable wisdom / goodness and love of the Triune GOD / in all living and essential creatures of the whole world and all their hosts / all of which were created, formed, and made in the beginning of time through the speaking and outflowing of His Eternal Word and the imperishable Spirit of His mouth; From which we learn / how the invisible and unspeakable GOD / with His infinite essence / has revealed Himself / and still reveals / communicates Himself and is present / through / and in all things / everywhere; Likewise how this Great and Holy God is Himself / and eternally shall be the Father and Provider of all His creatures / their Essence and Motion / Life and Food / Light and Refreshment / Teacher and Guide / in sum / the Beginning / the Middle and the End of all His works in heaven and on earth.

<header>and short Introduction.</header>

## Statement of the Author regarding his Writings.

This book rejects the books of all earthly men / and desires / after it has been read through once, twice, or thrice / and is rightly understood / to be rejected itself / so that the glory remains for **GOD** alone / who says there:
> I am the **Lord** your God / who teaches you what is profitable / Isaiah 48:17. <note>original: "Esa. 48: 17." # Author’s Preface.

<margin>1.</margin> The Holy Divine Scripture / the high and mighty living witness of the Almighty living **GOD** / addresses us all thus: *You err and do not know the Scripture.* <note>Matthew 22:29.</note> That is: we poor / blind / foolish people all ought to know this above all else / that the true knowledge of **GOD** is a living / active / Divine light / which does not consist or lie in a mere / earthly / invented delusion / or a brutish <note>The original German "Viehischen" (animal-like or carnal) refers to human understanding that has not been enlightened by the Spirit, operating only on a physical or "beastly" level.</note> dead word; as almost everyone since the time of the Apostles has, in terrible blindness, mostly held it to be. For immediately after their mortal passing, the true knowledge of God was almost extinguished / because we did not rightly observe or heed their writings / but <term>glossed</term> <note>original: "Glossiret." To gloss means to provide explanatory notes or interpretations. Sclei argues that these commentaries distorted the original meaning of the Bible.</note> them falsely and wrongly / and interpreted and pointed them toward a very different understanding / than the Apostles themselves intended / who all worked with the greatest diligence for this alone / so that the true living knowledge of **GOD** / might be propagated and preserved among us.

2. For since Christ our **LORD**, the living Son of **GOD**, thoroughly instructed them as his Apostles alone in the true knowledge of **GOD** / as He then explicitly gave us all to understand for further instruction with the following words: *To you it is given / to know the mystery of the kingdom of **GOD**: but to those / who are outside / everything happens through parables / so that seeing they may see / and not see: And hearing they may hear and not understand / lest they should ever be converted / and their sins be forgiven them.* <note>Mark 4:11-12.</note> Thus He intended to show us that we must not learn and grasp it anywhere else / but from the Apostles alone.

3. But because we reverse and confuse all things / never followed this faithful counsel of **GOD** / and despised his Apostles as dead men / and instead wanted to learn such things from living people / these same people have painted and fantasized such a **GOD** for us / as pleased and suited them / so that they might be raised up to high honors / and could better provide for and fill their bellies without hindrance; And all this they have taken not from **GOD** / but from their brutish reason.

4. However, the high Majesty of **GOD** is such an inexpressible and incomprehensible light / that it can never be reached or grasped by any human reason in eternity / according to the Scripture: *No one has ever seen **GOD**. The only begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father / he has declared him.* <note>John 1:18.</note> And therefore it is greatly to be lamented / that we have followed them so carelessly / and allowed ourselves to be so masterfully led astray / and took neither the Holy Scripture / nor the Apostles of **GOD** into counsel here / to see if these claims agreed with their meaning; because of this it has turned out so poorly / so that we [have lost] the living **GOD** / and his true knowledge entirely

He has also in three ways, paths, and manners—that is, in three books, in three writings and mirrors, or in three living images and alphabets—very wonderfully, richly, and abundantly revealed, depicted, and made known Himself, His Holy Name, and His unchanging good will to the whole world, but especially and primarily to His chosen ones. Thus, whoever has properly and thoroughly studied one of these three books, reflecting and seeking within it, would not significantly lack or fail in the true knowledge of **God**. However, if there be anyone who seeks the knowledge of **God** outside of these three books, he errs greatly and shall never find it rightly. And these three books are and shall be called the Living Book of the Living **God**. The first is the MACROCOSM <note>original: "MACROCOSMUS." The "Great World," referring to the entire physical universe.</note>, the second is the MESOCOSM <note>original: "MESOCOSMUS." The "Middle World." The "Little World," referring to the individual human being.</note>. These are the Great, the Middle, and the Small World.

<margin>9.</margin> The content of these three books is one and the same and agrees: This is it: The knowledge of **God** is eternal life. But eternal life is **God** Himself alone, without whom we cannot attain eternal salvation; however, we cannot have **God** without true knowledge, for He Himself is His knowledge; just as, on the other hand, the clay <note>original: "Leimen." <margin>10.</margin> Now, so that man—the creature of **God**, who is but clay—should not perish, die, and be destroyed eternally in such ignorance of **God**, Almighty **God** has presented these three living books as a mirror and as a light to the world—that is, to man, to the clay, to the darkness, to the ignorance—so that they should learn to know Him rightly therefrom. The first is Holy Scripture; the second is Heaven and Earth; the third is Man. And these are the three great books of **God**, and the mighty Triple Mirror of **God**, in which the inexpressible majesty of **God** allows itself to be seen visibly and tangibly; whoever will not look upon and grasp Him there will surely miss Him for eternity.

<margin>11.</margin> But the foolish-bold <note>original: "thumm-kühne," a combination of "dumb/foolish" and "audacious."</note> world despises these Holy books of **God** and boasts of its own great, self-grown wisdom, cleverness, and understanding; and out of this, its earthly, clay-like, beastly wisdom, it fills the whole world with its false books, so that the books of **God** are entirely forgotten because of them—so much so that Holy Scripture itself complains of this and says: *Of making many books there is no end.* <note>Ecclesiastes 12:12.</note> None of this would happen if the world rightly recognized these mighty books of **God**, which He Himself has written and prepared with His own finger.

Namely, how man should attain salvation and eternal life through the knowledge of **God**, for which purpose alone we were all created, provided we do not willfully exclude ourselves from it.

16. However, the true knowledge of **GOD** consists in the humble knowledge of oneself, and not in the investigation of unnecessary things. For if man could fathom that, he would actually be above **God**, and more than **He** is. But let it be far from us to think such a thing. To such people **Solomon** speaks not unjustly:

§ 17. But as for what **God** is? How He has revealed Himself, and from where our origin comes? To know this is not only not forbidden to us all, but is even commanded and permitted. For this is the will of **GOD**: your sanctification. **1 Peter 1.** <note>Specifically referencing 1 Peter 1:15-16.</note> Therefore **God** Himself addresses us thus: **Leviticus 20.** Be holy, for I am holy; I am the **Lord** who sanctifies you.

# The First Book
## of the General Doctrine of God;
### Concerning the Nature, Benefit, and Use of God’s Creatures, and to what end they are given to us.

---

<margin>1.</margin>
Since the eternal, Almighty **GOD**, who dwells in an unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6), had resolved within Himself to allow Himself and His **Holy Name**—that is, His eternal Essence and His good will—to be seen, and thereby to portray <note>The original German term *abconterfeyen* means to depict, sketch, or create a likeness, as in a portrait.</note> Himself and present Himself in an image: it pleased Him in His Divine Counsel to undertake this through no other means, way, or manner than through His *OPPOSITE* <note>original: "CONTRARIUM." A philosophical concept suggesting that the invisible God reveals Himself through His opposites: the visible, physical, and temporary world.</note>, namely, through the visible, the transitory, and the naught, so that He might thereby show and make known that He was all in all, and had need of no other.

2. This is now the creature <note>In the 17th century, "creature" (*Creatur*) referred to any created thing—animate or inanimate—within the natural world.</note>, the **Holy Scripture**, and the letters of **God**, which **God** has written with His own hand, and has thereby depicted Himself—showing that He is the eternal **God** and **Man**, outside of whom there is no other **God**, according to the Scripture: *I am the **LORD**, and there is no other; besides Me there is no **GOD**.* Isaiah 45.

3. For the Scripture, and the eternal, unchangeable good will of **God**, which from eternity [was] in... <note>The text ends mid-sentence; the catchword "dem" indicates the next page begins with "the."</note>

To this end, the eternal invisible God began to make Himself visible, and to bring forth in the creation of Heaven and Earth and everything therein, together with all creatures, which **God** created all for this purpose: that we should learn to see, fear, and recognize Him therein and therefrom, and thus might have our eternal joy and delight, rest and Sabbath <note>The term "Sabbath" here refers not just to a day of the week, but to the mystical concept of eternal rest and union with the Divine.</note> in Him without end, Amen.

5. To this I now speak thus: Everything that I see and do not see is God to me. For in His wisdom **GOD** has created all things. Psalm 104.

6. But against this, the wise Solomon says: All things are vanity and transitory. Ecclesiastes 1. That is: everything visible is unfit, void, fleeting, and perishable; how then can these two things be reconciled? <note>The author is pointing out a paradox: if everything in the world is "God" (as per point 5), why does the Bible also call the world "vanity" or "nothingness"?</note>

7. The Holy Scripture of God speaks wondrously of itself thus: Look upon the works of the Most High; they come in pairs, two against two, and one against one. <note>original: "zwey wieder zwey / und eins wieder eins." This is a reference to Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 33:15, reflecting a philosophy of dualism or polarity where opposites define each other.</note> This is not said of the Holy Scripture alone, but also of all other letters of God <note>The author views physical objects as "letters" or symbols in a book written by God’s hand.</note>, whether they be light or dark, empty or filled, dead or living. Therefore, if someone could rightly compare and unite these two contradictory points and conclusions founded in Holy Scripture, they would not be too far from the true knowledge of God. Sirach 33 verse 15.

This refers to the theological idea of the *Deus Absconditus* or the "Hidden God" who wraps His blinding light in darkness or physical matter so that humans can perceive Him without being destroyed.</note>, so that He might be seen and grasped therein, who otherwise remains incomprehensible and unsearchable to all men because of His immeasurable clarity. Ephesians 4. Psalm 18. 1 Timothy 6.

### Divine Doctrine / First Book.

9. Therefore, we must know before all things that the whole creaturely world and all created beings—but especially man—are nothing other than a birth of God, and without God, they are nothing.

10. This is essentially to say: **GOD** is all in all, and the creature is nothing. This is indeed a wondrous, yet a truthful and necessary saying.

11. For whoever wishes to be a true Christian must, before all things, know how to distinguish the perishable from the imperishable, the temporal from the eternal—yet without separating them; for whoever does not know this distinction, by what right can he be called a Christian? <note>The author suggests that a believer must recognize that while the physical world is temporary, it is still permeated by the eternal, and one must navigate both without losing sight of the divine source.</note>

12. The creature is nothing in itself and first took its beginning through the word *Let it be* <note>original: "Fiat." The Latin command used by God in the Book of Genesis to bring the world into existence.</note>; therefore it shall also pass away, but God and His word remain eternally. Therefore, we should hold fast to God and let the perishable go.

13. Therefore, everything that the creature now is, possesses, and is capable of, it has solely from God; thus it is not its own, but God's. And for that reason, it should use everything it is and has to the honor of Him from whom it received it, so that the name of God alone may be hallowed within it. For this is the end <note>The "end" here refers to the ultimate purpose or "telos" for which something was made.</note> of all creatures: that they are created for God's glory. Therefore, man should also direct his actions and life in such a way that God may be grasped and seen within him.

14. But man soon, while he was still in Paradise, shifted away from his goal and overstepped the *boundary* <note>original: "Terminum." From the Latin for a limit or boundary line.</note> of God's commandment, turning away from God—who is the eternal living Word itself—and turning inward toward himself; thus, through this, he immediately fell into the abyss of hell and died the eternal death. <note>In this mystical tradition, "hell" is often described not just as a place, but as a state of being separated from God and trapped within one's own self-will.</note>

15. Man’s turning away from God is the cause of all misfortune; therefore, he immediately fell out of Paradise and into hell; for he who does not stand in God, where else could he be but in hell?

16. If we were truly serious about this matter and believed the Word of God—that things are exactly as it reports—we would surely not remain idle or lazy. Instead, we would strive to the utmost to find our way back to our former state of rest. For in hell, no redemption is to be expected; it is found only in that place where Christ, hanging on the cross, comforted the thief: namely, in Paradise. <note>The "former rest" refers to the state of man before the Fall, a common theme in mystical theology where salvation is a return to an original divine union.</note>

17. Now, as to how this redemption happens, or by what means and way it is obtained, no one cares to ask. Although God has established and ordained means and ways and commanded us to walk in them, there is no one who puts this into practice. Instead, as the Scripture laments in Psalm 14, they have all turned aside and become useless together; there is none who does good, not even one.

18. As long as we walk in hell, all things are also unclean and evil to us, according to the Scripture: *To the wicked, all things are evil.* <note>The author interprets "hell" not as a physical location reached after death, but as a current spiritual state of being separated from God's grace.</note> For without the true knowledge of God, we misuse all things; for who can remember God in death, or who will praise Him in hell? (Psalm 6).

19. Therefore, it must finally come to the point where we recognize our misery and nothingness <term>Nichtigteit: the state of being "nothing" or "vain" without God's presence</term>, and consequently despair entirely of our own actions and omissions. We must hold only to our Redeemer and the salvation of God, so that God may again be all in all. That is: Christ must not suffer and die within us in vain; rather, it must serve our best interest and our redemption. That is: God must truly be born in us, rise, and reign, and we must thus enter into His glory through much tribulation and suffering. (Luke 24). <note>original: "Herzlichkeit." While this word now means "cordiality" in German, in this 17th-century context, it is used synonymously with *Herrlichkeit*, meaning divine glory or majesty.</note>

20. Of all this, our predecessors <note>original: "Vorgeher." This likely refers to the established religious authorities or previous generations of clergy who the author believes have lost the true path.</note> say not the slightest word to us, for they do not know it themselves. Therefore, they are not the redeemed, and they are not those who can rightly thank God and praise and exalt His mercy. (Psalm 107).

21. 22. 23. 30. That is to say: then they stand in **God** and not in themselves. 31. 57. 77. For what God gives us, that we have, and we also keep it, so that no man can take it from us; all the rest, what we have and learn from men, we do not truly have, for we cannot keep it, but it consumes us like smoke in the air.

# Teaching of God / First Book

78. How could miserable man—who is himself naked and bare and purely nothing—give anyone anything lasting, since he himself has nothing that is his own? And even if he had something, it would all be earthly, deadly, and transitory things that have no permanence, just as he himself is only earthly, beast-like, deadly, and mortal.

79. Christ, the Son of God, knows all this well; therefore, our misery, poverty, and nakedness <note>original: "nacket und bloß." In early modern theology, this imagery describes the "natural man" who lacks any inherent righteousness or spiritual merit before God.</note> move Him to pity. For this reason, He came to us on Earth and gave Himself to us as our own, if only we would accept Him. That is to say: He has given us His life-giving Word <note>original: "lebendigmachendes Wort." This refers to the Word of God as an active, creative force that spiritually restores the believer.</note> so that we might put it on to cover our nakedness and defend ourselves against all evil (Isaiah 62). But alas, there are very few who put it on like a garment.

80. For thus Christ speaks to us all in common, in *John 14: "My peace I leave with you."* This is truly a most powerful and unspeakable gift, which Paul explains in this way: *“Since we have now been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.” Romans 5.*

81. Is that not the same as saying: *“That which I myself am and have, that I leave to you; therefore, abide in Me and in My love, and I will abide in you.” John 15.*?

82. And for a further and more powerful confirmation, He repeats it a second time: *“My peace I give to you,”* as if He were saying: "Hold fast to this alone and to nothing else, for this alone is lasting and eternal, while everything else is transitory." And He Himself notes the distinction here, saying: *“The world cannot give you what I give you.”* Therefore, He concludes: *“I, who alone have everything in My power and in My hand, give it to you alone; and what I give you, no one shall be able to take from you.”*

83. How truly excellent and powerful a word this is for the one who builds upon it and rightly ponders <note>The catchword "bewe" indicates the word "beweget," meaning to move, ponder, or reflect upon.</note> it in his heart...

He must not mix one into the other, but learn to distinguish them properly and well from one another, clinging to the right foundation alone, and letting the false, mixed-in chaff and straw <note>original: *Sprew und Hexel*; agricultural metaphors for the worthless human additions that distract from the "grain" of God's truth</note> go as a harmful poison. For only the inner sense of the Spirit of **GOD** within the text, as it unfolds in the Bible, is **GOD’S** Word and the Gospel that has flowed from the mouth of **GOD** and from the Book of Life; this is the living power of God Himself. Of this, Paul and Solomon say: *Every word of God is fire-tested; He is a shield to all who hope in Him.* <note>original Latin: *Omnis sermo Dei ignitus: Clypeus est omnibus sperantibus in se.*</note> All the words of God are purified and are a shield to those who trust in Him. Proverbs 30. The Word of God is living and powerful and sharper than any two-edged sword, and it pierces until it divides soul and spirit.

58. Whoever now has this Name of God and knows Him, has eternal life. For He Himself is the eternal life. Now, no human lives on earth who does not have this Name of God within him; for in Him we must live, and without Him, who is Life itself, we cannot live. Therefore, the cause of our eternal ruin lies only in this: that we do not wish to recognize Him, but instead despise and surrender Him, and only take heed of the earthly and temporal, which is nevertheless perishable and cannot be counted for a single moment against the Eternal.

9. This transformation can happen nowhere else but while we are in the flesh <note>The author emphasizes that spiritual rebirth must happen during our earthly life, not after death</note>, which is the only thing God demands of us and works within us. But if we were to do this—avoiding the world and the external, and calling upon God for faith and enlightenment—He would open our eyes from day to day. We would then see with clear eyes how everything external is deceptive, false, and fleeting, and for that reason, we would cling to the internal alone. *2 Corinthians 3, 4, 6, 7; Galatians 5:6.*

10. Therefore, we must know and believe that there is another man within us: namely, a heavenly, eternal, and immortal man who cannot die but is eternal; whereas the outer man decays and comes to nothing. *2 Corinthians 4; Romans 7, 8.*

This refers to the theological idea that God works through paradoxes, hiding his favor under the appearance of his wrath.</note> through Hell into Heaven; through the Cross into glory; through death into life; through poverty into riches; through darkness into the light; through lack into all fullness; and through the humiliation of *Christ* into his exaltation with *Jacob, Joseph, Israel,* and *David*. 176. For God kills only for this reason: so that He may make alive again. *Deuteronomy 32:39; 1 Samuel 2:6.* He performs a <term>foreign work</term> <note>original: "frembd Werck." Otherwise, we stand in the way of God and ourselves through our own efforts; we hinder God so that He cannot come to His work of grace in us, nor unite us with *Christ* for eternal life, until He has first humbled us through His wrath and justice in the Law. He drives us away from our self-reliance so that, like poor sinners on the <term>scaffold</term> <note>original: "Scavott" (Schafott), a platform for public executions. ## An Introduction to the True Wisdom of God. <note>original Latin: "Introductorium in veram Dei sapientiam."</note>

# Summary of the Content and Concept of this Little Book.

This little book informs you in simplicity where, how, and in what measure, or by what means we may seek, find, and attain the true, essential, living <term>knowledge of God<note>original: "Erkantniß GOttes." This refers to an experiential, heart-felt awareness of the Divine rather than a purely intellectual or academic understanding.</note></term>, which until now has been unknown and hidden from the whole world for a very long time. Through this alone are we released and set free from our innate <term>brutish blindness<note>original: "Viehischen Blindheit." This terms describes a state of spiritual ignorance where a person lives according to animal instincts and earthly desires rather than divine light.</note></term> and from the false, fabricated, presumed, and dead knowledge of God, with which the whole world is now filled.

For it points us to Christ, our sole universal teacher of the truth of God; it explains and shows who He is and where He is to be found, while rejecting all men who teach and spread the Devil’s lies and fables.

<margin>1.</margin> GOD / the supreme Artist / who alone creates and does all things in heaven and on earth in Christ JESUS our Lord / according to the Scripture; "Whatever the Lord pleases, He does in heaven and on earth, in the seas and in all deeps." In this wonderful ANATOMY He rejuvenated, spread, multiplied, and made Himself grow so marvelously / that no end of Him may ever be found; so that He nonetheless remains the unique One in this manifold multiplication / and thus is all things and yet also Nothing / which then appears as the highest wonder to the godless world / which cannot find its way into the works of GOD / appearing marvelous and strange to them. And because they cannot fit into their mad heads / how this comes to pass / they neither will nor can believe it or be content with it; thus they become quite lost, confounded, and impatient / and turn away from GOD / and in this turning away they set themselves up as idols / doing whatever pleases them and seems good to them, contrary to the one true living God and His great / unspeakable WORD.

This refers to the movement from the divine Trinity (3) into the physical world of the four elements (4).</note></term> / and straightaway transmutes it into True Unity <note>original Latin: "Veram Unitatem."</note>. And thus He prepares, cooks, purifies, rejuvenates, multiplies, and brings to light His eternal Heavenly self-subsisting TRUTH within it. But the world / not content with this / wickedly presumes to be something more / and thus wants to be that which she is not. Yes, she even falls into such folly / that she presumes to be the **SPAGYRIST** and **ALCHEMIST** herself / to set, order, master, handle, and change all things according to her own pleasure / which in the Holy eyes of GOD is the greatest abomination and the highest blasphemy; therefore she is rightly rejected and cast away by GOD as a dull salt and a useless broken vessel. Concerning this, the Prophet speaks thus: "Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight," Isaiah 5. Woe to him who strives with his Maker, namely the potsherd with the Potter of the clay! Does the clay say to... <note>The text breaks off here at the bottom of the page.</note>

Let their eyes be darkened, so that they do not see.** Psalm 69. This is a truly terrifying judgment that rightly follows our ingratitude and negligence.

61. 62. 63. Now, the region of life is nowhere else but in the heart—not, however, in the brutish heart of man, but in the Heavenly Heart, which is to say, in the Heart of **GOD**, which is in Heaven and in Paradise, from which man has been cast out. However, so that we would not remain eternally in death, surrounded by darkness and ignorance of **GOD**—since we have been deprived of the face of **GOD**, from which alone all ignorance arises—God has once again, in a most wonderful way, placed us back into [the light]. # Of the General Doctrine of God /
<meta>catchword: for</meta>

He Himself is not only the food, but also the hunger and the steward <term>Speisemeister: a master of the feast or one who provides and distributes food</term>. He Himself is the prisoner, the prison, and the redeemer. He is the sick person, the medicine, and the physician. He is the sheep, the pasture, and the shepherd. He is the school, the student, and the schoolmaster Himself. All this has happened from the Lord and is marvelous in our eyes. *Ps. 118.* Therefore, blessed is he to whom God gives understanding of his prison, his sickness and infirmity, his yoke and his cross—which he is to carry after Christ, or rather, which Christ Himself carries within him—while he is still healthy and alive in the body, and allows him to truly recognize this. Even more blessed is he to whom God shows how he can be redeemed from it; and most blessed of all is he whom God has redeemed and set free from it, so that while he is still alive in the body, because he is still here on earth, he can already be in Paradise.

253. For repentance—that is, redemption—is not open to us any longer than as long as we live here on earth in our body. After our death, when we lose the body, it is completely finished. For out of hell there is no redemption, and where the tree falls, there it shall lie <note>A paraphrase of Ecclesiastes 11:3, commonly used in the 17th century to emphasize that a person's spiritual destination is fixed at the moment of death.</note>. Redemption can indeed happen while in the body, but after that, it offers nothing more; that is, no further redemption occurs outside of the body. For after our departure, the spirit returns to Him who gave it, and the body returns to the earth from which it was taken, according to the Scripture which says: *Go to the side of the holy world, etc. Sirach 17.* <note>original Latin: "In partes vade Seculi Sancti, &c. Syr. 17." The author interprets this as joining the company of the living who honor God.</note> 

This means: Hold yourself to the side of the holy world, to the living who give honor to God, and do not persist in the error of the ungodly. Confess <term>Beichte: In this historical context, this means both the confession of sins and the public acknowledgment/praise of God's power</term> before you die. For confession departs from the dead and comes to nothing; if you wish to confess to and praise God, you must do so while you are alive. While you are healthy and vigorous, you must acknowledge God and praise Him, and glory in His mercies. Here we hear clearly that we must provide for ourselves while still alive in the body; after our death, nothing will come of it.

...of the world's way to love darkness more than light (John 8), the flesh more than the spirit, and death more than life; rather, he should choose life for himself, so that he might live, and his seed with him (Deuteronomy 30). 269. We all indeed have eternal life within us, for without it no person can live on earth; however, we do not all have it in equal *possession* <note>original: possession</note>. For unfortunately, many have it only as a leased property <term>Lehens Gut: a feudal metaphor; property held from a superior lord rather than owned outright as one's own</term>, and this is true of the majority; but few possess it as an inheritance and as a personal property accepted through faith (John 1, 3, 6, 10, 15).

Now, those who do not hold it by inheritance, but only by lease, cannot possess it eternally; and from them will finally be taken even what they have, according to the Scripture: **And you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.** (1 John 3, Luke 16, 19, Hebrews 6). For whoever has eternal life in him and does not strive for how he might keep it eternally is a "manslayer" <term>Todschläger: literally a "death-striker," here referring to a murderer or one who commits spiritual suicide</term> and a murderer of his own soul. 

We keep it within us, however, through a persistent faith, reflection, contemplation, prayer, and spiritual breathing <note>Odemholung: a metaphor for constant spiritual renewal, like breathing in God’s grace</note>, and through love—when we carry it within us day and night, and thus tend to and care for the "prisoner" within us as is right, according to the Scripture: **Refresh the weary, and this is my refreshment.** <note>original Latin: "Refice lassum, & hoc est meum Refrigerium"</note> 

**This will be your rest, if you provide rest for the weary, and this is the refreshment.** (Isaiah 28). And thus God does not desire our negligence, as the Scripture says: **God did not make death, and has no pleasure in the destruction of the living.** (Wisdom of Solomon 1). <note>Sap. 1 refers to the Book of Wisdom, or Sapientia.</note> Even though He has led us into hell, He nevertheless does not kill us therein, but only lets us see what we are, and leads us back out again afterward, provided we do not resist Him ourselves; however, it does not happen without or against our will (1 Samuel 2, Hosea 6).

270. 273. What is the bitter death? It is man with his earthly wisdom and the senses and thoughts of his heart / through which he brings death upon himself / just as Adam did by eating from the tree of knowledge / in order thereby to become like God in the knowledge <note>original: Wissenschafft; in this context, it refers to experiential knowledge or mastery</note> of all good and evil. 275. So, if the external, bodily distress, fear, and danger that occasionally affects and unexpectedly falls upon us is so great that we are so intensely horrified and frightened by it, how much greater and immeasurably greater will the internal distress of the soul be? For we can ward off the distress of the soul far less than that of the body. And if we despise temporal distress, how much less will we rightly consider the internal, eternal distress? But who is it that can turn these both away from us, other than God alone through His Almighty Word? For if we poor human beings are not even able to still temporal hunger, how much less, and how very much less, will we know how to—or be able to—turn away or still the eternal hunger? For who is there among us all who, even if he filled himself to the brim with the most costly food, would not have to eat again on the following day? Indeed, the more he fills himself, the more and sooner he hungers for it again; and thus, as long as he lives here on earth, he cannot be satisfied. What then will become of such an earthly hunger in the hereafter? Truly, I fear that an unfathomable and unspeakable hellish pain will follow from it.

276. In short / today we regard, believe, and do nothing less than God's Word / as if the exact opposite had been commanded of us. Although the Devil and the world never preach, everyone nevertheless does everything according to Satan's word and the mind of the world. Who and from where does one teach and learn this? Should God not have power to teach us His Word just as well in the heart and to make us into **living books** of goodness / just as the Devil, world, and flesh drive us daily from within toward evil, even without external words and preaching?

### Of General Divine Doctrine

The overshadowing of God rests solely in His arm, in His Word, and in His Son, who represents and intercedes for us without ceasing with unspeakable groanings; for the angels of God ascend and descend Jacob's ladder without ceasing through our heartfelt sighing. This sighing is the true cry that pierces the clouds and caused God to answer Moses: "Why do you cry out?" <note>A reference to Exodus 14:15, where God responds to Moses's silent prayer during the crossing of the Red Sea.</note> This is what God the Father alone attends to and hears. Here it refers to primeval chaos or a formless heap.</gloss></term>.

309. Ask Him for a report of where He was before this time, where He is now, and where He shall go in the future; then one will be able to pass all the more securely with Him through this dark, gruesome valley to the place and the spot where he was before (with God) before the foundation of the world was laid. Jeremiah 1.** This is truly an excellent report, in which the <term>office<gloss>original: *Ampt*; refers to one's divine calling or duty in life.</gloss></term> of us all is contained. ## Second Part.

324. Therefore, now consider, O you miserable mortal man, your weakness and your great inability. # Of the General Teaching of God /

## Of the General Doctrine of God

381. Therefore, O dear human, take good heed that you remain a **good seed** and a **good angel**, for which God has created you, so that you do not <term>degenerate</term> <note>original: "degenerirest," meaning to fall away from one's original divine nature or kind.</note>. Pray to God day and night with David and the entire congregation of all the saints of God, saying:

> **Preserve me, Lord, for I trust in you.** *Psalm 16.*

> **Preserve my soul, for I am holy; save me, Your servant, my God, I who hope in You alone.** *Psalm 86.* <note>The word "holy" here refers to being "set apart" or "consecrated" to God through faith, rather than claiming personal perfection.</note>

Consider well that Christ the Son of God so faithfully warns us that we should watch, and not weigh down our hearts with <term>gluttony and drunkenness</term> <note>original: "Fressen und Sauffen," literally eating and drinking like animals.</note> and with the cares of this life (*Luke 21*). Rather, we should wash our garment—our soul—in the blood of the Son of God, the unblemished Lamb who has been sacrificed since the beginning of the world, so that this **testimony** might finally be shared with us, which all believers attain, and which reads thus:

> **These are they who have come out of great tribulations, and have washed and cleansed their garments in the blood of the Lamb.** *Revelation 7.*

382. Now, however, all things are in the eyes of God: the Word of God and the blood of Jesus Christ which flowed from His side, He who through His death and suffering has cleansed and blessed all things. For what else could there be in heaven and on earth that did not flow forth from the side of Christ stretched out upon the **Cross**, as water and blood? From where else could it have taken its origin? If we now recognized all things as being for the Word of God and for the blood of Christ, we would also wash and cleanse our garment, our soul, in this blood. We would use all things in sobriety and moderation, in the fear of God for **necessity** alone, and by no means for **excess**, which defiles us. But if we do otherwise, and misuse things in all manner of gluttony and <term>sow-like lusts</term> <note>original: "Saulüsten," a derogatory term comparing human appetites to those of a pig.</note>, and overstuff ourselves, we do not only defile ourselves, but we also transform the blood of Christ into a **beastly blood**. We thus shed innocent blood and become **murderers of Christ**. Should that not be a terrifying abomination before God?

## Second Part

Therefore, I earnestly ask the Christian reader that no one should think I am attacking or assailing the clerical estate <term>Geistlichen Stand: the clergy or those in religious orders</term> alone, or doing so too severely and beyond measure. Or that I am particularly targeting, slandering, injuring, or condemning one person or another out of hatred or envy; no, by no means. For such a thing is fitting for neither me nor any other in this manner, for the reason that we are all stuck in the same condemnation; therefore, it is said of us all:

> You shall not condemn, so that you are not condemned.

**Matthew 7**. You should know, however, that I am here treating a **Universal Theology** <note>original: *Universalem Theologiam*; a theology of general spiritual truths applicable to all people</note> and not a **Particular Theology** <note>original: *Particularem Theologiam*; theology focused on specific sectarian dogmas</note>, which is why I have titled or named this little book thus—not for the sake of glory, but rather forced by necessity. I do this so that I might not be viewed with suspicion by those who rightly understand the matter; as for the ignorant, I care nothing for what they will say of this, for it is a very small thing to me that I should be judged by a human day <note>This refers to 1 Corinthians 4:3, meaning a human court or human judgment as opposed to God’s judgment.</note>. From this **Universal Theology**, however—which only **Christ** and his **Apostles** and **Prophets** have rightly treated, and especially the **Evangelist John**, who also 
<margin>1 John 5.</margin> says thus:

> The whole world lies in wickedness.

Absolutely no one is excluded, and thus no one can be excluded by me here either; yet few are willing to see, grasp, and take this to heart, not even the wisest and most learned. Therefore, I trust in **God** that I will not offend or do wrong to anyone with this, because I mean all of us equally, one as well as the other, just as the **Holy Scripture** and **God** himself thus punish each and every one, none excepted, so often and so harshly. And those who first and most of all accuse and judge themselves in their faith also—with the word and judgment with which they judge themselves—afterwards rebuke others through the **Spirit**, who even today rebukes the whole world regarding sin, righteousness, and judgment. **John 16**. And thus, no one will rightfully have cause to complain against me. **Isaiah 9, 56.**

### Third Part. 425

...words, these words of Christ should also be understood: **Take and eat; this is my body.** For just as God, out of eternal paternal love, has given us His Son and everything in and with Him, so now it is our work that we, as children, receive and eat everything in and with Christ through faith, so that we may be satisfied, rich, wise, great, and magnificent in God, from the rich treasures of His house, and thus be filled with all the fullness of God.
<margin>Isaiah 25, 55; Psalm 36.</margin> <note>The original OCR lists "Ef.", which likely refers to Esaias (Isaiah) rather than Ephesians, as chapters 25 and 55 of Isaiah describe the divine banquet and the invitation to eat and drink of God's grace.</note>

In this way, Adam and his descendants had their eating and their food blessed and sanctified once more; yet it was quite secretly concealed, so that the Devil could no longer perceive it—namely, in the hope of the future Redeemer and Savior, in whom they believed. Through such faith in His words, they were turned back to Him from their fall and restored.
<margin>Genesis 3.</margin>

And it is just as if God had said: Death and life are simultaneously hidden in all things, and to Me they are essentially one thing. Life is death, and death is life. And if we thus find life in death, and can live in the midst of death, we then become like God again in Christ, and dying then becomes our gain and life in Christ.
<margin>2 Corinthians 4; Philippians 1, 2, 3.</margin>

12. Therefore, everything depends solely on the command, or the commandment and prohibition of God; that is, on the gracious good will and the love of God. When that is overstepped, death is already there and present. For this reason, the children of men should do nothing of themselves, but only that which God commands them; everything else is an abomination in His holy eyes. 65. ### Third Part

And the bread that we break, is it not the **communion** of the body of **Christ**? For we, being many, are one bread and one body, for we all partake of one bread and one cup. <note>A translation of 1 Corinthians 10:16–17. What then can a rich **idolater** <note>original: *Abgötterer*; here referring to someone who worships their own appetite or status through food.</note>—who makes an idol of both himself and his food through his misuse—prepare for himself other than the bread and the wine, the flesh and the blood, which the poor man has just as much as the wealthiest, except that the rich man sins much more greatly with it. Woe to him, however, that he so misuses it; why then does he boast so vainly? And so blasphemously? And so hideously? With the precious gifts of **God**.

75. All excess, however slight it may be, is nonetheless a sin against **God** and an indisputable **idolatry**, and moreover, a murder and manslaughter in the holy eyes of **God**. For what else does he do with it, when he so overfills himself that he no longer knows himself, than that he:
1. Kills **himself** with this deed.
2. Subsequently kills **others** with his evil example, by giving them a pattern to do likewise.
3. Thus he also kills his **poor neighbor**, from whom he withdraws [sustenance] by this [excess].
4. He also kills ***Christ* himself** in His gifts, which is a truly terrifying fourfold manslaughter. <note>The author posits that gluttony is not just a personal sin, but a violent act against the self, the community, the poor, and the divine presence within the food itself.</note>

Besides this, he mocks **God** in heaven, just as the *Jews* did in the wilderness, who also said: **Can God prepare a table in the wilderness? Can He also give bread and provide meat for His people?** For they did not believe in **God** and did not hope in His help. They tempted **God** continually and provoked the Holy One in *Israel*. *Psalm 78.* <note>Referring to Psalm 78:19–22, where the Israelites are rebuked for doubting God's provision despite the miracles of the Exodus.</note> Is it not true? The gifts of **God**, as **God** has given them...

## Supplement on the Practice of Prayer / and the Mental Sabbath-Rest or Spiritual Death / in order to attain the New Rebirth.

Every believing or baptized person in Jesus Christ / has put on Jesus Christ / and thereby agreed and sworn / to deny three things / that is / to die to three things during their life ; through the help of the Holy Spirit in faith in Jesus Christ. The first is the lust of the flesh / or worldly desires / according to the "old man" <note>A biblical reference to the unregenerate human nature before spiritual transformation.</note> / which / if they remain in a person / they bring eternal death / for they war against the soul. The second is the lust of the eyes or Mammon / and all kinds of perishable goods / so that he might separate his heart from them / and go out from the love of people / be it father / mother / brother / sister / wife / child / friend / <term>etc.</term> / and live in Jesus Christ alone. The third is a prideful life / that is / that he would also hate and lose his own life / for Christ's sake ; even if he should be despised / mocked and scorned / persecuted and hated / indeed even killed by the most shameful death for Christ's sake / so he would not love his life even unto death / but willingly give it up for Christ's sake. Such is yieldedness <term>Gelassenheit: a central term in German mysticism referring to a state of perfect detachment and surrender of the self-will to God</term> / or faith / that is love / or the true knowledge of Jesus Christ : Whoever cannot let go of these three things / but possesses them with a sense of ownership / has no faith / does not know / what faith or love is / and denies the suffering and life of Christ. Everything depends on love / or on the death of Jesus Christ within us / by which true Christians are to be recognized. Where this yieldedness is not practiced / through faith / as through the Word / which has become flesh in us / there Christ is denied with his suffering and life / and the *mystical symbols* <note>original: "Mystische Symbola"</note> / or *sacraments* <note>original: "Sacramenta"</note> / [when used] in unyieldedness / where lust of the flesh / lust of the eyes and a prideful life rule over the soul / used in unbelief / they lead to judgment / 1 Corinthians 11.

### Third Part.

Keeping the Sabbath, according to God’s command, is the gentle death of Christ—a sweet and blessed dying in Christ, in which our inherited death dies away from our soul, and the soul receives a new body from Christ’s flesh and blood, in which there is no corruption, sin, or death. The more often you earnestly keep this Sabbath, the more you escape the great creaturely world and its evil stars <note>original: *bösem Gestirn*; referring to the early modern belief that the fallen material world was governed by celestial influences that affected the unredeemed human temperament</note>, and your heart becomes completely changed. From a greedy, angry, envious, haughty, filthy, and lustful person, one becomes a gentle, mild, truthful, pious, humble, moderate, and holy person through Christ within. This is what it means to lift the mountain and cast it into the sea—both of which are within us—that is, to uproot the tree from the field of Adam <note>original: *Acker Adami*; the "field" of fallen human nature inherited from the first man</note> and transplant it into the new field of Christ within us, so that the worst of the old birth, the Devil, and the world cannot harm us.

Therefore, after heartfelt contemplation of your innate Adam-like misery <note>original: *Adamischen Jammer*; the wretched spiritual state of humanity after the Fall</note> and after your penitent, heartfelt sighing and prayer, surrender yourself often to a silence <note>original: *Silentium*</note> or stillness; honor God and keep the Sabbath. There you will become aware of the idols in your mind, will, and desire, which you have served—how they pull at you and do not want to let you focus on the Lord. You must then let them fall from your senses into oblivion. Let God come to you from within and without; forget yourself, so that God may find place and room to work and to enlighten you. There you will come to such a light, day by day, that you will surpass all your teachers of reason. There God's commandments will become sweeter to you than honey and the honeycomb, and you will taste the Kingdom of God within you. For there are two kinds of sweetness: a human one and a divine one. The human sweetness is active <note>original: *wircklich*; here meaning based on human effort, such as external religious rituals</note> and creaturely, coming from reading, hearing, and praying; but it does not last long and has no roots. The divine sweetness is passive <term>Passive (leidentlich): In mystical theology, this describes a state where the soul stops its own activity to "suffer" or receive the direct action of God.</term>, where a person waits for God in a stillness and, like David, hears what the Lord speaks within him. This brings roots and eternal power, and is a superhuman sweetness that one can never for-

# Of General Theology /

...forgotten; in this way, one might become an inward person and learn all things in the school of God, of the Holy Spirit, without effort or toil.

But there are many beginning people, says that mystical teacher <note>original: "I. T.", referring to Johannes Tauler (c. 1300–1361), a famous German Dominican mystic and theologian</note>, who wish to fly before they have grown feathers, and want to pick the fruit before it becomes ripe and perfect. Therefore, as soon as such beginners have started a good life, they immediately want to fly up high through the contemplation of divine and eternal things, chasing after that which they cannot yet grasp. For these people, it is very difficult to contemplate the bitter suffering of Jesus Christ (it is too bitter and too sad for them); they do not want to trouble themselves with it, nor do they want to follow the humble footsteps of His humanity. Consequently, their state is very precarious, and they are in great danger regarding their salvation; for whoever does not enter through the door of the humble, surrendered <term>Gelassenheit</term> <note>A central concept in German mysticism meaning "yieldedness" or "letting-be"—a state of perfect detachment and submission to God's will</note> humanity of Christ can never reach His divinity. 

This happened to a priest who in no way wanted to concern himself with the noble humanity of Christ; contemplating His suffering became bitter to him. He wanted only to occupy himself with the high divinity, which he could not, however, comprehend. Now, while he imagined that he stood quite securely, he fell; and in that fall, he recognized his true nature to its depths <note>original: *zu Grunde*; literally "to the ground," but in mystical writing, it refers to the *Seelengrund* or the deepest "ground" of the soul where God dwells</note>. Then he began to speak: "Oh, eternal, merciful God, I now realize, alas, that I have done wrong, for I did not want to go through the humanity; therefore, I could not and was unable to reach the height of Your divinity. For if I had directed my way to go through You in complete surrender and humility, and had thus followed the pure image of Your holy life, suffering, and death, I would not have fallen so. Therefore, whoever wishes to come to the high divinity, into Life, must enter through the lowly humanity of Christ and die with Him, so that he may attain the life without end."

This is the perfect great Name of the one Living God / in His Holy Highly-Praised Trinity. Now, whoever does not grasp and recognize the Creator in the Father / and the Redeemer in the Son / and the Enlightener in the Holy Spirit / can say nothing yet of a Living God / and to him the words of Christ are rightly cast as a reproach / which read thus: *You err and do not know the Scripture / nor the power of God,* Matthew 22. Now, although the works of the Holy Trinity of God are distinct / and divided / they are nevertheless so distinguished and yet so connected / that they are and remain entirely and perfectly inseparable / for even though to each person His own special operation is assigned / yet the operations remain together as one and united in <term>Concordance</term> <note>original: "Concordanz"; referring to the harmonious agreement and unity of action between the three persons of the Trinity</note> and not two / just as the persons also remain together undivided eternally. 2. <meta>Following the title page of Dr. Bartholomew Sclei’s 1596 "Sermon on Repentance," this page provides a table of contents or a summary of the work's core theological argument. It introduces the mystical concept of the "Triple Word" and the "Concordance."</meta>

## Content of this Sermon on Repentance.

This little book deals with and treats the manifest, visible, and tangible revelation of JESUS Christ. In doing so, it teaches what the <term>Creature</term> of God—the **Triple WORD**, CHRIST the Lord, the Son of the living God—actually is.
<note>original: "Creatur"; here, the author refers to Christ’s manifestation in the created world or the "Word made flesh," rather than a "creature" in the sense of a common animal.</note>

Namely, the **CONCORDANCE**, that is, the Essential living God Himself, whom the world does not see, know, or recognize, who thus disguises Himself, and yet reveals Himself so wonderfully to **HIS OWN**, who seek Him in His **WORD**; which wonderful Word is therefore called and named the Trinity of God because it is threefold and yet one.
<note>original: "CONCORDANZ"; a technical term in this context referring to the mystical harmony or essential union between the divine nature and the created expression of the Word.</note>

In this wonderful, threefold, living Word, the high, incomprehensible Majesty of **GOD** alone lets Himself be truly seen, heard, felt, found, grasped, and held, and in no other way or means. And although today many are found, even among the most prominent, who seek **GOD** in a defiant, insolent, and perverse manner where He is not: Namely, in the **false Nothing** (in their own human thoughts), they nevertheless make a mistake, deceiving both themselves and many others alongside them; therefore they also find nothing and keep **NOTHING**; that is their deserved reward, and they rightly suffer want eternally.
<note>original: "falsche Nichte"; likely a critique of philosophical or abstract spiritualism that attempts to find God through intellectual "nothingness" rather than through the specific person and Word of Christ.</note>

Therefore David says, not without cause: Lord, I have loved the habitation of your house, and the place of the tents of your glory.
Ps. 26. <note>Psalm 26:8</note>

It warns readers against seeking God in abstract "human thoughts" (the "false Nothing") rather than in His revealed Word.</summary>

# General

The Prophet David says to Him:
> Lord / look upon me / and have mercy on me / for I am lonely and miserable / the anguish of my heart is great / deliver me from my distresses. <note>original: "Ps. 25. 16."</note>
Ah, truly / my dear sirs / do you not yet know where that single, humble little word "Solitude" <note>The author emphasizes "Einsam" (lonely/solitary) as a spiritual state of humility and isolation from worldly corruption.</note> leads? If you all / who are supposed to teach others / do not know this yourselves / who then will be among the simple, unlearned crowd / who might recognize and consider their own failings and sicknesses; of which David speaks thus:

# Sermon on Repentance

Do you truly think you will fall? Tell me then, how do you know? Truly, into a very dark and unclean corner, where the noble wine and the precious beer, and the many fine morsels—which the poor must now constantly carry after you—will taste quite strange to you; so much so that I fear you will tremble greatly because of it. Where do you think you will fall then, when the LORD of Hosts <note>original: "HERR der Heerschaaren," a traditional title for God emphasizing His power over all heavenly and earthly forces.</note> shall snatch away from under you his throne, upon which you now parade as if you were entirely alone, and give it to another? Truly, I say to you, into eternal darkness (unless you do penance), where fine wines, fine morsels, and precious refreshments will no longer please you, but rather there will be howling and gnashing of teeth; there you will have to suffer want for it eternally. <margin>Psalm 33</margin>

17. You highly enlightened gods, who boast that God speaks with you alone and with no other common man, and that this Scripture refers only to you: I have said, *You are gods*: <note>A reference to Psalm 82:6, "I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High." Rulers often used this to justify their status, but the author uses the second half of the verse to humble them.</note> How are you so forgetful that you do not consider what follows and sounds like this: *And children of the Most High, all of you*: This little word **All** is a great word that excludes no one. How then do you come to this opinion, letting yourselves imagine that it must be applied to you alone? Has not God likewise poured out His Spirit over all flesh? Why then do you remain silent about what follows? Oh, do not let yourselves dream that it is you alone; the others belong to it as well, and they are the rightful heirs who shall remain when you must depart, even though you now despise and persecute them. But perhaps you mean to imply by this that you are the ones who do not know the only begotten Son of God, JESUS, but rather separate and deny Him; yes, dear sirs, forgive me, but it is true: you are the very ones.

21. Consider then, for God’s sake, where was David, the great and mighty king in Israel, when he spoke such bitter words to God? Surrounded by precious adornments? And yet, the abyss within him caused such words to be heard from him. Was he not in his own flesh and blood, in which we all still remain this very day? How is it then that we do not also cry out to God with such words and persevere for deliverance as he did? Only unbelief causes us to be dead and to carry death unknowingly around our necks <note>original: "am Halse tragen," a figure of speech meaning to be burdened by or constantly threatened by something</note>. # General

<page-num>554</page-num>

CHRIST the Lord did not pray for us without cause: "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do" <note>Luke 23:34</note>. Therefore the Spirit of God accuses them thus in Isaiah 28: 
> All tables are filled with vomit and filth, so that there is no more room; 
> both priest and prophet are mad from strong drink, 
> they are drowned in wine and they stagger. 

This concerns them alone, and is spoken against them, for they alone are the ones who sit at the table, eat, and banquet, interpreting the Scripture according to their own heads. All the others must suffer the loss and be their **foot-cloths** <note>original: "Fußhader," a rag for wiping feet, symbolizing something lowly and trodden upon</note>; and if they wish to eat, they must search for and pick up the crumbs under the table, waiting for what is thrown down to them from the pulpit. See and hear, for God's sake, what a gruesome name He gives to their preaching and teaching! And this is because they lack **Concordance** <term>Concordanz: literally "harmony"; here referring to a lack of inner consistency or alignment with the divine Truth</term>, and they themselves do not know what they are saying. That they preach would not be something to scold or blame in itself; this, however, is to be blamed: that they venture to do so outside of Concordance, while they completely lack the **Anointing** <term>Salbung: the "unction" or spiritual empowerment of the Holy Spirit which traditionally authenticates a preacher</term>. 

But so that we would not become aware of this in them, and could not point out and reproach them for this lack and infirmity, they blind us beforehand and deal with us so very mildly and gently. They give us smooth, oily words (Psalm 55) and speak only what we like to hear. They paint a picture of a gracious God for us and say: "Peace, peace, and security; we have made a covenant with death, and with hell an agreement" <note>Isaiah 28:15; original "Pact" from the Latin *pactum*</note>. No one needs to fear misfortune—even though the Lord says: "The wicked have no peace at all" (Isaiah 48).

62. Meanwhile, while they blind us in this way, they live, gorge, and guzzle, entirely hardened in **pride** <term>Hoffart: an archaic term for high-mindedness or vanity</term> and greed. to you, you wretched man; for the sake of your miserable refreshment, you know no better solace than that which the grace of God provides you, for in this way you will not taste the sweetness of God nor savor His supper. <note>original citations: Ps. 34:8, "Taste and see that the Lord is good"; Luke 14:24 regarding the Great Banquet</note> Woe also to you, that you study in such a way and lead the Holy Spirit into your school, forcing Him to speak and insisting He must say what you want, and **imitate** <note>original: *imitiren*</note> your style—a style you draw from another lying bellows <note>The "bellows" refers to a false source of inspiration or "hot air," contrasting with the true breath of the Spirit.</note>. Instead, it lasts even to this very day, and finally reaches until the end of the world, continuing until we have all come through. For we all should and must still go through it, just as all the Jews before us had to go through; for there is otherwise no other detour, neither behind us nor before us. Therefore, our entire life in the eyes of God is and is called a pilgrimage, a passage, a **crossing** <note>original: *Transitus*, Latin for a crossing or passage</note> and **Passover** <term>Phase: derived from the Hebrew *Pesach*, referring to the "passing over" or the journey of the Exodus</term>.

63. For Death and the Devil still wait for us this very day to do their service, seeing if they might ambush and creep up on us, to sink us and drown us; for they still stand to this day on both sides, like the literal walls of the Red Sea.

### Penitential Sermon

[...in] your body and in your spirit, which are God's, who prepared the body not without cause in the form of a cross and as a member of Christ, and created it for His temple. 1 Corinthians 3, 4. <note>The author references 1 Corinthians 3:16 and 6:20, suggesting that the human physical form itself—often compared to a cross when standing with arms outstretched—is a divine design intended to house the Spirit.</note> It is indeed true that Christ, in His birth, made us all kings and priests, for that is exactly the **birth of God**; however, this birth does not occur without suffering and pain, therefore it cannot be without the cross, otherwise it would be no birth.

103. For all people who wish to attain salvation must be born twice: once from the physical mother and a second time from the **heavenly Mother**; therefore, well is it for him who recognizes his heavenly Mother—the **spiritual Mary**, Christ’s **Church of the Cross**, and the **free Jerusalem** which is above—and holds her in honor, and follows and obeys her in all things with the true children of Zion. Galatians 4, Revelation 12, 14, Hebrews 12. <note>The "Spiritual Mary" and "Jerusalem above" are mystical symbols for the womb of spiritual rebirth or the true, invisible Church.</note> May he thereby be preserved from the love of the false harlot and the wisdom of **Babylon**, according to Proverbs 7, 8, 9, and Revelation 17, 18. <note>Babylon here represents worldly corruption and false religious systems.</note> Now, this is not a wooden cross, or such a one as the hypocrites wear on their cloaks <note>original: *Gleißner*; a biting critique of those who wear religious symbols like the cross of a military order or crusader without internalizing the sacrifice</note>, but a very different cross indeed. For through this living cross of **CHRIST**, through the **rebirth** (which extends until the death of the flesh, and is finally and truly confirmed, completed, and concluded with death), we must enter the Kingdom of God and be finally anointed as kings and priests by God the Holy Spirit Himself in the **third baptism**; and all of this must happen here on this earth and in this life, being completed through the **triple baptism** of Christ. <note>In this mystical tradition, the "triple baptism" refers to the progression through water (repentance), the spirit/fire (enlightenment), and blood/suffering (the death of the self).</note> Whoever does not reach this birth of God while he lives here on earth will not attain it there (if he willfully neglects it) but will be cast into the uttermost distress. (Ah, in what great distress and danger stand all the clergy who understand none of these baptisms, even though it is their sole office commanded to them by Christ in Matthew 28 to reveal such things to the world.) For thus shall and must the passion of the suffering of our Lord Jesus Christ, without ceasing, throughout our whole life...

# Penitential Sermon

...what then must His birth be? Will it not also fill heaven and earth? Indeed, since the birth of God fills heaven and earth, will it not follow that the great and mighty presence of God surrounds us everywhere, whether we are in heaven or in hell? This point is contrary to all worldly reason, which views it with suspicion and denies it. <note>The author is arguing for the omnipresence of God, suggesting that "the birth of God"—likely referring to His creative and sustaining power—exists even in the depths of hell, a concept that challenges standard logic.</note>

105. O, how blessed we would be if we believed this! For this reason, David says: *If I ascend into heaven, You are there; if I make my bed in hell, You are there also.* (Psalm 139). Therefore, the inexpressible love of God toward all people can be clearly measured by this: that He will leave us helpless nowhere, neither in death nor in life. For the singular birth of God causes every corner to be full of God and to contain Him. Yet there is no one who sees Him, recognizes Him, or knows how to find Him rightly, to thank Him properly for these great mercies. Therefore, it is deeply to be lamented and incessantly mourned that there is no one who wishes to hear, see, or recognize **JESUS CHRIST THE NAZARENE**, hanging stretched out on His own cross, though He cries out to us with a mournful voice day and night: **My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken Me?** <note>original: "Mein Gott / mein Gott / warumb haſtu Mich verlaſſen." This refers to Christ's cry of dereliction on the cross (Matthew 27:46), here presented as a perpetual call to humanity.</note> If we took this voice of His to heart or recognized it, we would also feel its power within us; but because we all run aside on the broad path according to our own whims, following foreign gods—as our fathers did, so do we—there is no longer any help for us, especially since no one wants to believe that Christ alone is the Physician of Israel, to whom we should all cry out: **Lord**, heal me, and I shall be healed; sprinkle me with **hyssop**, and I shall be clean. (Jeremiah 17; Psalm 51). <term>Hyssop: A plant used in ancient Hebrew purification rituals for cleansing the sick or the ritually impure.</term> If we did that, the streams of Living Water proceeding from Him would cleanse and sanctify us, according to the Scripture (John 7): All those to whom this water comes have been healed. For this very same unique Physician is the one who comes to us with water and blood, and not with water alone...

...[not alone], but with water and blood—that is, with body and soul—not imaginary <note>original: "Phantastisch"; referring to a mere mental concept or an illusory appearance</note> but substantially <note>original: "Wesentlich"; meaning in actual essence or reality</note>. 106. Therefore, Christ speaks even more abundantly: "Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves Me; and I will reveal Myself to him. Now, whoever knows that the Word proceeds from the Father and is His only-begotten Son loves it as perfectly as the Father Himself and is also obedient to Him. To this, Judas Thaddeus <note>One of the twelve apostles, often identified with Jude</note> asks: "Lord, how is it to happen that you will reveal yourself only to us and not to the world?"—as if he wanted to say: "Since You are the great and mighty, sole Universal Light of the entire wide world, why then will You not also enlighten all the world alongside us?" To this objection, Christ answers: "The world cannot receive the Spirit of truth, and this because it neither sees Him nor recognizes Him. For if someone loves Me, he will also keep my word." That is to say: the world is too clever and too wise in its own eyes; therefore, it follows its own reason <term>Vernunfft: human intellect or logic operating independently of divine revelation</term> more than **God's** word and will. Because my word is too despised and too lowly for it, and the world rejects it and will not recognize it for what it is, I cannot help the world outside of that word. For I am **God**, who can neither lie nor change, as you humans do (Malachi 3).

# Preface of the late <note>original: "seel." (selig), a term used for the deceased, meaning "of blessed memory."</note> Master Abraham von Franckenberg regarding this booklet /
## which was sent to press by him in the year 1639.

->Grace from GOD and peace in our Lord JESUS Christ.<-

1. Inasmuch as / Christian and in GOD devout dear reader / this writing has come into our hands without the name of the Author or other information / except that it was transcribed in the year 1595 in Little Poland <note>original: "Klein Pohlen" (Małopolska), a historical region of Poland that was a center for religious dissent and reform during the 16th century.</note> / and as it appears / it may perhaps have belonged to Dr. Bartholomew Sclei <note>A physician and religious writer associated with the mystical and spiritualist movements of the time.</note> (whom we mention in the appendix) or to another theologian well-practiced in the Sanctuary of the Lord.

2. And we have likewise noticed / that many useful and wholesome teachings and reminders concerning **PRAYER** and other edifying Articles of Faith are contained therein / which in today’s cold-heartedness are almost entirely forgotten. Thus we have deemed it necessary to give such a work to the public press for the benefit of the Community of GOD: So that the negligent may be exhorted all the more to prayer / and the unpracticed in the spirit of truth may be fruitfully built up and taught by GOD : To which end we then most faithfully wish them Divine blessing and prosperity from above / and for the sake of greater attention and devotion / we briefly set before your eyes the contents of this booklet.

3. Accordingly, the Spirit testifies through the Author from a true Concordance <note>A "concordance" here refers to the harmonious agreement between different sources of truth.</note> of Holy Scripture with the **Book of Nature** <note>The "Book of Nature" is a theological concept suggesting that God's will and character can be read in the natural world just as they are read in the Bible.</note> / entirely Universal and impartial.

4. I. That **GOD**, **WORD**, **SPIRIT**, Name, Power, Sum, All and in All **CHRIST** / Spiritually, Physically, and Essentially works, is, and dwells.

<summary>Abraham von Franckenberg introduces a 1595 manuscript discovered in Little Poland, which he is publishing in 1639 to revive the "forgotten" practice of internal prayer and spiritual devotion. He attributes the work's wisdom to the harmony between the Bible and the "Book of Nature," emphasizing Christ's universal presence.</summary>
<keywords>Abraham von Franckenberg, Bartholomew Sclei, Little Poland, prayer, Articles of Faith, Book of Nature, spiritualism, 17th-century theology, mysticism</keywords>

# Preface.

5. II. That **PRAYER** is **EATING** of the **WORD** of the **LORD** / without which—as the true Essence of all beings—no creature is able to live nor remain in its being. And for that reason, all creatures groan with us for the **BREAD** and **WORD** of Grace: as well as the Word in the Bread and the Bread in the Word / namely, the **Body of Mercy in the Body of Justice**, and the **Body of Justice in the Body of Mercy** <note>original Latin: *Corpus Misericordiae in Corpore Justitiae, und Corpus Justitiae in Corpore Misericordiae*. This refers to the mystical union of God’s compassion and His righteous judgment within the person of Christ.</note>, as the **BODY of CHRIST** and His **BLOOD** / are essentially hidden in a mysterious way in all things.

6. III. That one should and must worship no creature / whether in heaven or on earth / but alone the **One GOD** in **Three Essential Persons** / in spirit and in truth / spiritually and physically / inwardly and outwardly: And serve **HIM** / as the Lord of all things / for and in all things / and give Him the glory.

7. IV. That the **SPIRIT of CHRIST** alone is the one / who, united with GOD the Father and the Holy Spirit / seeks and finds / honors and worships / Himself within Himself / effectively and essentially / and for that reason also obtains and receives the hearing of prayer in His own and no other Name / from Himself / in Himself / and through Himself. Provided that we believe / that **CHRIST**, with His Spirit and gifts, wills to work and dwell through faith in our spirit and heart.

8. V. That **Holy Scripture** / as well as all of **NATURE**, is the great book closed with 7 seals <note>A reference to Revelation 5:1, symbolizing divine secrets that can only be opened by Christ.</note> and the testimony of the Lord; to be contemplated with fear and trembling / and to be careful not to misuse or dishonor the Name and the Word of the Lord / nor the creatures created from and placed within it / so that we do not awaken His wrathful countenance against us—as the fire of judgment / which lies and works hidden in a **seed-like and sacramental manner** <note>Franckenberg uses "seed-like" (original: *Saamentlicher*) to suggest that judgment is a latent potential within the world, and "sacramental" (*Sacramentlicher*) to suggest it is an outward sign of a hidden spiritual reality.</note> / and be consumed and extinguished by it / as can be seen from Holy Scripture and other well-known histories and examples.

<summary>In this section of the preface, Franckenberg defines prayer as a spiritual nourishment and warns that God's presence is hidden within both Scripture and the natural world. He emphasizes that true worship occurs through the Spirit of Christ dwelling within the believer.</summary>

## The Contents of this Book.

This little book treats and discusses what the "call" and prayer are, and what that is which prays or eats there—namely, the <term>Continual Sacrifice</term> <note>original: *Juge Sacrificium*, referring to the perpetual daily offering in the ancient Temple</note>, the wondrous <term>Cohobation</term> <note>original: *Cohobation*; in alchemy, this is the process of repeatedly distilling a liquid over its own solid remains to purify it. Here, it refers to a process of spiritual refinement and rebirth.</note>, the wondrous sacrifice of God: **CHRIST** the Lord Himself on the <note>original: *Ara Crucis*</note> **Altar of the Cross**, who shows and gives Himself so wondrously to His own. For the image, the sacrifice, and the birth of God—the eternal life, which eats itself and is God Himself—that very thing is nothing other than the new creature, or new birth, which stands and arises in the Lord's Supper. Within this, the most dangerous, difficult, and doubtful point, **ON THE PREDESTINATION OF GOD** <note>original: *De Prædestinatione Dei*</note>—concerning the eternal providence of **GOD**—is very comfortingly elucidated, explained, and perceived. We are all obligated to learn and recognize this point rightly, so that we do not provoke the eternal curse upon ourselves, which reads thus:

> Let their table become a snare before them, a retribution, and a trap. Let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see, and make their loins tremble continually. Psalm 69.

...the way of the wicked shall perish, because the Lord alone knows the way of the righteous. <note>A continuation of Psalm 1:6 from the previous page.</note>

12.
