# Of the Lord’s Prayer

A Prophet <note>Likely referring to the author of Psalm 89, Ethan the Ezrahite, regarded here as a prophetic voice.</note> who has seen and recognized this great ignorance, darkness, and presumption of ours in the spirit, makes himself heard before God with a lamentable, pitiful voice, thus: **Remember, Lord, what my essence is; have you then created all the children of men in vain?** Psalm 89.

15. Truly, if we knew and understood rightly what eating is, and what the slaughter of the fatted cattle signified <note>A reference to the Parable of the Wedding Feast in Matthew 22</note>, and what the invitation to the wedding in the Gospel contained within itself—also why we were invited, and why we must eat—we would not allow ourselves to be served so richly and superfluously beyond measure. We would not so over-gorge and fill ourselves with unnecessary, harmful food and drink, worse than any filthy sow, but would gladly let a small and meager portion suffice for us. For hidden within eating lies the death and the suffering of Christ, and the unspeakable mercy of God, which we cast away from us when we so shamefully abuse God’s gifts of food and drink, as the majority of people in all the world do now. And as long as we do not learn to understand this rightly, we remain stuck in God’s wrath and disfavor, and cannot perfectly obtain the mercy of God, much less sing or sound it forth with the Apostles and Prophets of God. How many of us will there be then, who will sing with David thus: **Because Your mercy is much better than the life of all men, so shall my lips praise You.** Psalm 63. I fear there will be very few of us; therefore he rightly complains and says: **I am solitary and alone, until I pass by.** Psalm 141.

16. Truly, one's hair might stand on end, and the whole body should rightly tremble at the great evil of the terrifying abuse of God’s food and Christ’s suffering, if only there were someone who considered it rightly. For we abuse not only the creature <term>Creature: Here meaning "created things," specifically the plants and animals used for food</term>, but the Creator Himself, who thus rejuvenates Himself and opens His power through miraculous means; that He alone is the life, and thus is—

He is also the food itself, who imparts to us the fear of God and feeds us with Himself. And woe to us, if we do not all eat the fear of God. Primarily, however, this word points to the fact that in all things we should hear, honor, and acknowledge God and not man, or any other creature <note>In this context, "creature" refers to anything created—people, animals, or objects—as opposed to the Creator.</note>, according to the Scripture: **You shall worship God your Lord and serve Him alone.** <note>original: "Du solt GOtt deinen Herrn anbeten und Ihme alleine dienen."</note> Deuteronomy 6:13 <note>The source text cites Deut. 6:10, but the quote corresponds more closely to verse 13.</note> and Matthew 4:10. ### Reflection ###

40. Now, he who eats rightly and knows what he eats also prays rightly, believes rightly, and acts rightly; but he who believes wrongly and does not recognize, know, or see what he believes or eats can start nothing correctly, no matter what he might do. For exactly what a person believes is also what he eats, and what he eats is what he believes, whether he likes it or not. Therefore, not everyone can eat rightly, and that is because they do not believe rightly. To this, St. Paul says: **Faith is not everyone's thing** <note>original: "Ding oder Speise" — literally "thing or food." Paul's sentiment is that not all have faith.</note> and provides the reason: **for not all obey the Gospel, Romans 10.** Instead, only those who submit themselves to the Gospel eat rightly and believe rightly; of all the others, not one does. Everyone should take this well to heart.

In summary: whatever a person desires, longs for, hungers and thirsts for—whatever they take pleasure in, with which they pasture their senses, and which stills, satisfies, fills, and calms their heart—that is what the person "eats." And that is his **GOD**, his faith, his bread, and his highest good for which he prays and which he worships as his god. It is the food in which he delights, just as an ox delights in grass, a pig in the husks, a miser in money, a <term>self-learned man</term> <note>German: *Selbstgelehrten*. This refers to those who rely on their own intellectual prowess or "head-knowledge" rather than spiritual revelation.</note> in books, a child of the world in worldly pleasures, and every person in that which pleases him and seems best according to his own mind—or that in which he finds his life's pleasure and gladly lives, exists, and rests, like a fish in water, as if it were his ultimate goal at which he aims.

Thus, the believer eats and drinks in all things the **Bread of Heaven** and the **Water of Life**, as Christ’s holy flesh and blood. The unbeliever, however, eats the curse, the judgment, death, and damnation. Since we are created in such a way that we all must eat, Christ the Lord says to us all: **Work for food, not that which perishes, but that which remains into eternal life (John 6), which the Son of Man will give you, for God the Father has sealed that same food.** To this He further says: **He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in Me and I in him; He who eats Life, eats me.**

§ 1. All this comes to them from the fact that Christ spoke such words to them, which read: **"He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in Me, and I in him. John 6."** God help us! ## Reflection

1 Cor. 8. Therefore, this prayer, eating, or sacrifice proceeds from God alone, through God, and in God. It is called a sacrifice and prayer because all our food and drink should be taken with great reverence and honor, with the invocation of the Holy Name of God, in fear and trembling, moderately and soberly, according to the Scripture. Ps. 2: Serve the Lord in fear and rejoice before Him with trembling.

70. For we do not offer this food to ourselves, but to God; the little word "Serve" bears witness to this. For He is the one who hungers—namely, the prisoner within us <note>The "prisoner within" is a common mystical concept referring to the divine spark or soul trapped within the fallen material body, awaiting liberation.</note>. This one eats within us, and He will finally call us to account one day and ask: whom did we serve? Whether we fed Him or our own belly? What kind of food did we set before Him? Whether it was chaff, husks, or wheat? Whether we were His servants or servants of our own bellies. Well then, it will be better for the one who has lived soberly and moderately at all times, and has not burdened his Guest with excessive eating and drinking. For this Guest of ours lets Himself be fed and satisfied with very little; He does not require costly courses and various dishes, Luke 14. He is content and takes kindly to what one gives Him, even if it were only dry bread, as the Holy Scripture testifies here and there. Therefore, He does not wish to be overwhelmed or stuffed, for He is no fattened pig <note>original: "Mast-Sau."</note>, nor is He a weakling <note>original: "weichling."</note>; the world does not want to believe this. And for this reason, eating and food remains a hidden, great miracle and a deep mystery of God in the eyes of all earthly, animal-like people, and is likely unknown to the greatest part of the world. Though it would be right that this—as the only means of true rebirth <term>Wiedergeburt: the spiritual process of being born again into a divine state</term>—should be known to all the world. But as long as it is so terribly abused, it is quite impossible for the world to come to the new birth.

71. Therefore, there is almost no one who has a right knowledge of what the new birth is, or in what it essentially consists. The world, together with its leaders <note>original: "Vorgehern," referring to spiritual or worldly authorities.</note>

93. **AND LEAD US NOT INTO TEMPTATION.** <note>original: "NE NOS INDUCAS IN TENTATIONEM"</note> Here we also pray for this much: That when GOD allows us to recognize that we have fallen into temptation, that GOD would not leave us stuck therein, nor let us sink or drown, so that the pit of the abyss does not shut its mouth over us eternally. Psalm 69. And therefore, blessed is he who constantly considers that we are placed here in this time solely upon a trial, to test what is **fixed or unfixed.** <term>fix oder unfix; likely an alchemical or metallurgical metaphor common in this period, referring to what is permanent and purified (fixed) versus what is volatile or transitory (unfixed) in the soul</term>. Therefore, we should not be safe for a single moment without the special overshadowing of the wings of God. Psalms 35, 63, 91. For without the overshadowing of GOD, all our doing and leaving <note>A common German idiom "Thun und Lassen" meaning all our actions and omissions</note> is nothing other than an offense and a tempting of God etc., and a descent into hell. Therefore we may well pray: **ABBA, dear Father**, do not let us consent to the temptation of Satan, who hunts us daily to turn our backs to your face; let us much less remain therein; but convert us to you, and preserve us steadfastly until the end, so that we never fall asleep in death, but end blessedly in you, Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. No one wants to recognize or consider this danger of the trial; people do not believe it to be as hard as it is made out to be, and thus they know how to excuse and talk themselves out of it quite politely everywhere. They also say it is impossible for a poor **layperson** <term>Leye; a person without formal theological training or clerical status</term> in spiritual matters concerning GOD and **salvation** <note>original: "Seeligkeit"</note> to come as far as the **learned scholars**; as if GOD were only the God of the learned, and had completely and utterly forgotten us laypeople. But GOD is not a God of the rich and the proud, of the wise and the learned of this world, but of the poor and the humble, of the infants and the simple, who are rich in GOD.

### The faith, living knowledge, and confession of all true Christians.

Oh, what a deep knowledge of the true living God he possesses, who knows and believes that God, the Trinity, the faith, and all things, are and act; and recognizes all such things in the fear of God itself within himself, sets them above and into work.

For whoever wishes to know God rightly must know Him in His works; whoever does not know Him in His works does not have the true God either; whoever boasts of God and yet denies His works wanders far, deceives himself and others, and is himself the "non-god" <note>original: "Nichtgott." A term for one whose concept of God is a hollow idol rather than a living reality manifested through action.</note>.

Just as God is conceived and born in all things, so He also suffers and dies in all things; therefore He also rises from the dead in all things.

Thus the Single, True, Essential God rules, lives, and governs, eternally and without end, both hidden and manifest in all things, and is Himself all things: to Him alone, and to no foreign god, be praise, honor, glory, thanksgiving, and majesty for eternal times, without end. A M E N.

<margin>1.</margin>

hidden in the darkness. For the external stands only in
the invisible Eternal, which alone carries and sustains all things,

Good alone is the everlasting truth of **GOD**, of **JESUS CHRIST**,
with which **GOD** has gifted and honored us out of grace;
to this we should and must hold fast in faith,
if we wish to inherit eternal life.

# The Fifth Discourse.

## EVERYTHING IS A SACRAMENT.
<note>original Latin: "OMNIA SACRAMENTUM"</note>

### How all things are a sacrifice of God or a mystery.

§ 3 Every person shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt, Mark 9. This is a very strange, wonderful, and hidden speech of Christ the Son of God; therefore, it is highly necessary for us to contemplate it daily. It indicates, however, secretly and covertly, that all things are a sacrifice of God, in which sacrifice the Son of God offers and presents Himself to His Heavenly Father as a sweet fragrance through the Holy Spirit. Who would now be so bold as to find fault with the sacrifice of God, even if it be ever so small, especially since the Scripture says in Psalm 50: *The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. A broken and a contrite heart, God, you will not despise.* Psalm 51. <note>The author cites both Psalm 50 and 51, likely due to differences between the Latin Vulgate numbering and other translations; both refer to the famous penitential prayer of David.</note> Who then would also despise or misuse even the least and most unworthy thing? Who would not much rather honor and worship it in God, in pure love and fear of God? Truly I say to you, all things are given to us to be hallowed and not to be misused, for **CHRIST** is the Sabbath <note>The "Sabbath" here is interpreted not just as a day of rest, but as Christ Himself, in whom the soul finds its true rest and hallowing.</note> which God has commanded us to hallow; He is now the whole creature, that is, every human being. Therefore, the Scripture says further: Every person shall be salted with fire

Among all the sacrifices of God, man is the holiest and most noble sacrifice; therefore, he must be salted with fire—that is, baptized from heaven with the fire of the Holy Spirit, and thereby be made into a heavenly sacrifice. When that has happened, so that he burns, ignited from above, he is then transformed by the heavenly fire into a <term>Salt-Ash (Saltz-Aschen): An alchemical and mystical term referring to the purified essence or "body" remaining after a substance has been refined by fire.</term> and prepared in such a way that with this salt, all other sacrifices can, may, and shall be seasoned and salted. This is what it means to truly hallow the Sabbath, for the creature is the Sabbath of God. <note>In this mystical tradition, the "Sabbath" refers to the state where the human will rests, allowing God to work through them; the "creature" (the created being) becomes God’s place of rest.</note> O eternal, merciful GOD! And yet they nonetheless insolently presume to baptize and teach others. ## The Sixth Discourse.

### Concerning the Mystery of our Redemption, on the Feast of the
### Holy Birth of JESUS CHRIST.

<margin>57.</margin> All those to whom God Himself has revealed and made known His mysteries from His own Heavenly School in His own person, and thereby redeemed them from the darkness and error of the hellish spirits—they know how to speak of the great-powered, secret <term>Wonders (Magnalien): From the Latin 'magnalia,' meaning the mighty acts or great works of God.</term> and miracles of God in a much different and higher way than the highly-learned and the ambassadors of this world. Therefore, they not only deceive themselves and err mightily in their own persons, but they also miserably lead astray the poor congregation of God alongside them. For they, the godless despisers of God, have all risen so high in their malice and in their pride that they leave nothing at all entirely unblemished; they do not let the eternal works of God and His great-powered wonders be and remain what they are, but instead confuse, destroy, and break them, and bring them to naught. # Sixth Spiritual Meditation

<meta>catchword: Phan-</meta>

...must be a past, mere history, of which nothing remains but the bare memory; which is a terrifying thing to hear, since these mysteries are and remain an everlasting truth of God eternally, according to the Scripture: *He has commanded His covenant forever.* <note>original: "Er hat geboten ſeinen Bund in oder zur Ewigkeit." From Psalm 111:9.</note> But all this they do, says Christ the Lord, because they do not know Him who sent Me; and because they have never yet truly tasted the true, essential knowledge of God, and do not yet know what God is, much less what His work is, according to the Scripture: *For they do not regard the deeds of the Lord, nor the work of His hands.* <note>Psalm 28:5.</note> Therefore, they cling only to the external, bare, and dead <term>letter (Buchstaben): The literal, outward reading of scripture devoid of spiritual life.</term>, and have never truly considered or meditated upon the inner, hidden Spirit of God, which is eternal life itself. Consequently, out of necessity, they are unable to interpret and explain these great and mighty, wonderful mysteries of God in any way other than how they themselves are—namely, earthly, temporal, and perishable. And if they have only observed and celebrated these <term>festivals (Festa): The liturgical feast days of the church calendar.</term> externally with their dead ceremonies and animal-like <term>antics (Gauckelwerck): Literally "juggling" or "buffoonery," used here to mock empty religious ritual.</term> with enough pomp and grandeur—filled with bawling and shouting and useless chatter—they then imagine they have done their part and performed everything quite well.

58. But God, who is a God of the living and not of the dead, pays no heed at all to the "dance of the dead" <note>original: "Todtentänzer" – a reference to the 'Danse Macabre,' here used to mock theologians who focus on dead rituals.</note> these people perform and drive among one another; for He looks only at the heart, according to the Scripture, Jeremiah 5:
> Lord, your eyes look only for faith.
Everything else that proceeds from unbelief and a false heart is a total abomination in His holy eyes. For all their doing and leaving is nothing other than a perversion of the works of God, whereby they interpret, stretch, twist, and turn them according to their earthly understanding. Is this not a right fulfillment of the Scripture that says:
> The fool says in his heart, there is no God. <note>Psalm 14:1.</note>
Do they not master and measure all things according to their own heads? Do they not put the inside out and the outside in, thus confusing all things without distinction, as if it were a minor, trivial thing known to everyone? Yet in truth, it remains an unutterable and incomprehensible mystery of God for all eternity—not only to these "coarse asses" <note>A common Reformation-era insult for those perceived as spiritually dull or stubborn.</note> but even to all the saints of God—which God has promised to reveal only to His own who love and fear Him. He wills that it be held dear and worthy by them as a noble, precious treasure, according to the proclamation of the angel to the poor shepherds:
> Behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. <note>Luke 2:10.</note>
Yet even so, they do not shrink from darkening the eternally shining and enduring wonders of God, which they attempt to "enlighten" and explain with their false glosses, <term>postils (Postillen): Published collections of sermons or biblical commentaries.</term> and commentaries.

59. But all this the wicked despisers of God, those coarse and senseless asses, will not recognize or consider at all; instead, they drum their own thoughts, lies, and darkness into the people...

## ON THE ESSENTIAL PRESENCE OF THE LIVING GOD IN ALL THINGS.
<note>original: "DE ESSENTIALI PRÆSENTIA DEI VIVI IN OMNIBUS"</note>

### Concerning the Essential Presence of the Living God in all things.

66. Hear, O you children of men! A common Latin proverb in the 17th century suggesting that the natural world is a mirror of the divine.</note> For the whole world is so full of blindness and darkness that, regarding the true knowledge of God and His **Essential Presence** in His Trinity, it still knows or understands nothing certain or fundamental from Holy Divine Scripture to this very day. Truly, it is no lie, and more true than the world can believe, that man does not know his one God and Creator in the slightest, much less knows how to name Him rightly, and least of all calls upon Him rightly; instead, he departs far, far away from Him and wanders about in error like a lost sheep, or like a blind man groping for the wall. But one cannot persuade the blind world of this until it hears and grasps it from God's Word itself, which only happens when God shows it to you, and when God Himself touches the heart.

67. Therefore, know from this point forward from God's Word that everything we hear, see, feel, and touch is the one, true, living, **Essential God**, hidden and present in the three persons of the Holy Trinity; for God Himself is the Trinity, according to the Scripture: *That which you see and hear. Acts 3.* <note>original: "Quod vos videtis & auditis. Act. 3." # The Seventh Spiritual [Meditation]

GOD spits into the earth and makes clay from it; He places this upon us, and by it we become seeing and praise GOD. <note>This imagery refers to the healing of the man born blind in John 9, where Jesus used saliva and dust to create mud for the man's eyes.</note> In the end times, all these mysteries of GOD and the great **mighty deeds** <note>original: "Magnalia"</note> of the entire holy **Trinity** <note>original: "Trinitåt"</note> will be rightly revealed. Then, for the first time, all things will be alive and speaking. For then all boastful, lying mouths shall be stopped; and conversely, the mouths of the mute shall be opened, and they themselves will boast of, proclaim, and recount the honor of GOD. 

For now, we are only in the sixth hour, when the weary JESUS sat by Jacob’s well and rested, and there revealed his wonderful mysteries and himself to the Samaritan woman and made himself known. And when it comes to the seventh hour, the fever will leave the sick. <note>The author contrasts two biblical stories: the "sixth hour" encounter with the Samaritan woman (John 4:6) and the "seventh hour" when a nobleman's son was healed of a fever (John 4:52), using them as metaphors for stages of spiritual revelation.</note> But now, and before this time, all things are dull, mute, blind, and dead—even man himself—until his appointed time. But blessed is he who arrives before this time; for from the time of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and those who take it by force seize it. Matt. 11. <note>Matthew 11:12.</note>

72. For we should know this: that year, time, and hour are one and the same to GOD. Therefore, every person can have now—if they only wish it—what they might hope to have "there" <note>Meaning in eternity or the afterlife.</note>. All of this will finally happen to us here on earth and in this life, and will by no means be left out; for GOD is faithful and true, and He wants to give it to us here if we only ask Him for it, and not save it until the future eternity. There, the waiting would be too long and the door would be closed. Therefore, the time is still outstanding and in the future, yet it is already beginning to dawn and look in upon us, if only we would pray diligently: *Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open and bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together. I, the LORD, have created it.* Isaiah 45:8. <note>original: "Esa. 45. 8."</note> For He who is to come will surely come and will not delay. In the meantime, the righteous shall live by his faith. Heb. 10. <note>Hebrews 10:37-38.</note> 

Therefore, blessed are all those who wait for Him, who are not secure and sleeping, but awake and hoping in Him alone, Amen. At present, we cannot and will not yet believe that the Word of GOD is GOD, and moreover our **Messiah** <note>original: "Messias"</note>, **Christ** <note>original: "Christus"</note>, and the Son of GOD, whom GOD sent to us as a **mediator** <term>mediator: a go-between or reconciler between God and humanity</term> to redeem the world. If we rightly believed this, we would already be perfectly helped; for GOD is the Word, and the Word is GOD. This appears strange and very wonderful to the world; it cannot find its way into this truth and does not want to believe it. For the world does not consider or know what it is that speaks there—namely, the mouth of the Lord alone, which is GOD the Lord Himself, according to the Scripture: *You have seen Him, and it is He who speaks with you.* John 9. <note>John 9:37.</note>

73. Everything that is spoken of GOD is interpreted solely as the Word, which GOD Himself is alone; for there is no other GOD to be found outside of this single living Word, neither in heaven nor on earth. This single Word is JESUS the **Nazarene** <note>original: "Nazarener"</note>, the only Savior of all the world. Whoever knows Him cannot easily be led astray. For it is precisely herein that all **error** <note>original: "Irrthumb"</note> lies hidden: that we [see] **MESSIAH, CHRIST, or JESUS**...

# Meditation

...the **NAZARENE** <note>original: "NAZARENUM"</note> to be who He is; that is, that we do not recognize the Savior of the whole world, and think that this is [another] Christ or a false Christ. Matt. 24. For Christ is a Miracle-Worker, and has a wonderful name, and is called **Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, the Everlasting Father, a Prince of Peace**. Isa. 9. <note>These titles from Isaiah 9:6 are central to the author's argument that Christ's nature is multifaceted and divine.</note> He is a Son of the living God, of the Most High, whom no one recognizes unless the Father shows Him to them; no other human being will rightly show and reveal Him to us, but He reveals Himself to His own in the **breaking of bread**. <note>A reference to the disciples on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24), who only recognized Jesus during the meal.</note> Therefore, he alone is blessed who rightly knows Him and hopes and builds upon Him, for His wrath will soon be kindled. But blessed are all those who trust in Him. Ps. 2. Whoever calls upon Him in faith shall not be put to shame, according to the Scripture: Upon Him shall His crown flourish. Ps. 132. So that He shall sing with the angels: **Glory be to GOD in the highest**.

74. Two things lie within us and sleep: one is the fear of God, the other is sin, and each is awakened by its own kind. Sin is awakened and made alive through evil company and through our own thoughts, which we take and draw from ourselves, and this is the **false nothing**. <note>The "false nothing" refers to a mystical concept where self-centered thoughts are viewed as having no true reality or spiritual value compared to God's reality.</note> For we are all forbidden to live in ourselves, but rather alone in God. The fear of God, however, is awakened and made alive through the thoughts of GOD, which is the Holy Divine Scripture. Therefore, our whole life from youth up to old age, and even into death itself, should be nothing other than a rejuvenation and rebirth to life and not to death, to good and not to evil; but we turn the page and become the worse the older we get. Everything that man is and has belongs to God and not to himself; therefore, he can rightly claim nothing for himself, but everything is and remains God's, who alone is all in all. But where man claims for himself that which is not his, he becomes an idol and a **Lucifer**; <note>Lucifer is used here as the ultimate example of pride—claiming God's glory and gifts as one's own property.</note> yet if he recognizes that he is only a servant and a **steward** <note>original: "Schaffner"</note> of it, he cannot be the master to whom everything belongs, along with everything the servant is and has. If the servant now recognizes that he has nothing but what his Master gives him, he makes nothing his own, but lets everything be and remain His who is its essence and who gave it: so that all glory remains God's alone. Therefore the **Light** that we are and have must be lit solely by the Light of GOD; but if we wish to light it from men, or from ourselves, we darken it much more than we enlighten it. Therefore those enlightened by GOD say: **The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?** Ps. 27. Therefore they fear no man, for they know that no man can either give them or take from them this Light; and even if the outer letter <note>The "outer letter" refers to the physical text of the Bible or external religious forms.</note> is taken from them, the kernel and the treasure remain firmly rooted and hidden in their hearts, which no thief is able to steal.

# Seventh Spiritual [Topic]

...must learn to recognize from **GOD**; for all things are externally **CHRIST** and internally **JESUS**; <note>original: "ideo Christus Creatura & Creator Jesus"</note> therefore Christ is the Creature and Jesus the Creator. <note>The author uses a mystical distinction here: Christ represents the outer, created form or manifestation, while Jesus represents the inner, eternal divine power.</note> If you now recognize yourself to be a letter of **GOD**, then look well to whether the living Spirit of **GOD** also rests and lives within you; otherwise you are nothing but a black, dead letter, <note>A "dead letter" refers to religious knowledge or scripture that is read but not spiritually felt or lived.</note> an offense, a deceiver, and an Antichrist. Furthermore, take note and recognize that you are a fallen spirit. Now, however, **GOD** lets you be born into the flesh out of grace, not so that you should practice all pride and arrogance, but that you alone fulfill the holy will of **God**. But so that you might complete all this so much better, **GOD** has presented His Word, His will, His arm, His help to you as a mirror, from which you can and should take the strength and power to put such things into action (according to the Scripture: In and with **GOD** we will do deeds, Ps. 60). From this you should see, hear, and recognize that you have a gracious and not an angry God. Without this power and help, you will be able to accomplish nothing, according to the Scripture: Without me you can do nothing, John 15. But in Him we are capable of all things, according to the Scripture: I can do all things in and through him who strengthens me, Phil. 4. In and with my **GOD** I can leap over walls, Ps. 18. In **God** we will perform virtues, Ps. 108.

76. So that you may see clearly and grasp it, and thereby be abundantly convinced that **GOD** has no pleasure in your ruin, nor in the ruin of any person—much less has any guilt in it—according to the Scripture: As I live, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he turn and live, Ezek. 18, 33. Rather, He wants you to live and to choose life; therefore He reveals His heart to you, so that you may know that He stands ready and waits to receive you at every moment. If only you will turn to Him from the heart, cease from your blasphemy, recognize the time of your visitation <note>The "time of visitation" refers to the specific moment or opportunity God gives a person to repent.</note> and not neglect it. And this His great mercy and redemption you find recorded in His Son, in His living Word, ready to help you, if you only give Him faith and consent, fight over such faith, and hold yourself firmly to it alone, and love it from the heart; then you are already healed, and you have what you believe, as the words state, according to the Scripture: Trust, or be of good cheer my son, your faith has helped you. This good will of God stands contained in His living Word and was founded from eternity, before the foundation of the world was laid, so that no one need doubt it. Since **GOD** has found us in hell, and still finds us in it daily—as in truth it is no different—then for **GOD’S** sake consider who you must be, and soon perform earnest repentance, believe the Gospel, the speech of **GOD**, the Son of **GOD**, who is in the bosom of His Father; for God does not jest with us, He is in great earnest, and He lets nothing cost much; His death has redeemed us all, according to the Scripture: For God has not appointed us for wrath, but to inherit salvation through our Lord **Jesus Christ**, 1 Thess. 5. For as many and all of us as are born into this world—

# Meditation.

...[already redeemed] and set free; provided only that we do not willfully and intentionally bind ourselves anew and plunge into damnation, but rather constantly remain in Him until the end, where we are placed—namely, in the Word of Christ (1 Thess. 3 & 1 Pet. 2).

**77.** Therefore, the highest treasure and comfort that a person can or may have on earth is this: to know that **GOD** has placed His Holy Name within them, and that the person themselves is and can be that very thing, by virtue of the **birth of God**, <note>A mystical term for spiritual rebirth or the indwelling of the divine nature in the soul.</note> if only they themselves desire it and do not let it be lacking on their part, according to the Scripture which says:
> Because he desires me, I will deliver him or help him; He knows my name, therefore I will protect him. He calls to me, so I will hear him, Ps. 91.

And thus a person is the Name of **GOD** themselves; for the Holy Name of **GOD** alone is all in all things, according to the Scripture:
> **LORD** our Ruler, how mighty, glorious, or wonderful is your Name in all the earth, Ps. 1. <note>The author cites Psalm 1, but this text—"O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name"—is found in Psalm 8:1.</note>

We are duty-bound to worship this single Name of **GOD** alone in all things, as the only Essential, living God, according to the Scripture:
> I will praise your Name for eternity, Ps. 86.

Christ also taught us to pray this way:
> Hallowed be thy Name,

not *our* name; therefore, a person should be careful not to undertake anything improper or un-Christian, so that they do not soil, pollute, or profane the holy Name of **GOD**, both within them and outside of them. For without the Name of God—which alone is the life in a person, which works, acts, walks, and lives, and is eternal life itself—the Earthly mortal man is nothing but a **dead carcass** <note>original: "todtes Aas"</note> and a **dead dog**, dust and ashes; we see this plainly in the corpse of every person.

**78.** Therefore, a person is duty-bound to live at all times, every hour and moment, in the **fear of GOD**; for he has and carries nothing else, nor can he live in anything else, than in the unspeakable holy Name of **GOD**, so far as he remains, lives, and works in Him (Joh. 15, Act. 17). If he then knows, names, and calls upon Him, then he will in turn be carried, protected, and shielded by Him in all distress, and finally be redeemed from all evil through it. For **fearing GOD** is also a **craft**, <note>The author describes spiritual discipline as a "Handwerck" (handiwork or trade), suggesting it is something to be practiced and mastered like a skilled profession.</note> and among all other crafts it is the very best and the very highest: Of which Christ the **LORD** Himself says:
> Blessed are your eyes, that they see, and your [ears] that they hear, Matt. 13, Luc. 10.

Those who now do not know God, they all lie caught in a twofold prison: But those who know Him and call upon His name, they alone are the redeemed. Finally, amidst all our good days, highest prosperity, and blissful state, we are in such great need that no human can help us out of it except **GOD** alone; for we lie among the poor in the highest poverty, but no one wants to recognize this; God have mercy, Apoc. 3. <note>A reference to Revelation 3, likely the message to the Laodiceans who believe they are rich but are spiritually "wretched, pitiful, poor, blind and naked."</note>

Eighth Spiritual [Meditation]

# The Eighth Meditation.

## WE ARE ALWAYS DYING.
<note>original: "SEMPER MORIMUR"</note>

### How our life is nothing else but a continuous dying.

**79.** What is man then, or what does he do upon the earth? Every person should direct their aim toward knowing what they are—namely, that they are nothing, they are capable of nothing, and they can do nothing, for they are dead and living-dead. Man is born into this world for death and for dying, so that he may die in the **LORD** and not in himself; for such a dying is actually a **rebirth** <term>Wiedergeburt: a central concept in German mysticism referring to the spiritual awakening where the old self dies so Christ can be born within the soul</term>. Therefore, he should do nothing else but die, so that God may live in him and fulfill His work in him (2 Corinthians 4, Galatians 2). 

Since he is born for death and dying, he should apply all diligence to die in the **LORD**, in God, and not in himself, in his carnal lusts <note>The original German "Säulüsten" literally translates to "sow-lusts," a vivid term for base, animalistic desires</note>, or in spiritual death; rather, he should die in the will of God. For the natural man is himself "death," and only through this "dying away" in the **LORD** is he first, in a wondrous way, redeemed from eternal death and made truly alive. When a person stands in God in this way, only then does God truly rest in him and keep His **Sabbath** and His **halcyon** <note>original: "Halcyonische." Referring to the "halcyon days" of ancient myth, this denotes a state of profound, supernatural peace and stillness in the soul</note> birth within him. For in this dying and spiritual sleep, God proves His great wonders and **mighty works** <term>Magnalien: from the Latin "magnalia," meaning the "great things" or magnificent deeds of God</term> of redemption or **rejuvenation** <term>Verjüngung: literally "making young again," referring to the restoration of the soul to its original, uncorrupted state</term>—that He is the one who leads us through death into life and raises us from the dead. This is possible for no one else but God alone; on our own account, we would have to remain eternally in death, were God not to lead us out wonderfully (Romans 6).

**80.** And so it is certain that a person does nothing else but die—if not in God, then in himself; for in death, one can do nothing else but die. Therefore David, even to this day, prays so fervently with all those who belong to him: "Lighten my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death" (Psalm 13). His word is an eternal word, which truly must be considered with right earnestness. For a person diminishes every hour and moment, even while he is growing, and thus consumes himself, just like a heap of coal-fire into which the wind blows. 

Therefore he must have a daily supply and **replenishment** <note>original: "Bususse" or "Buße." While usually meaning "penance," in this context of food and drink, it refers to the physical "restitution" or "making up" for the energy the body loses</note> of food and drink if he is to reach the goal set by God and carry out what is commanded of him—namely, to know God and **do penance** <term>Busse: both the physical act of restoration and the spiritual act of repentance</term>. For the human body has a consuming fire within it just like all other things, and it must be maintained through the addition of its like, just as all other things are maintained in and through fire—namely, through a heavenly, **invisible fire** <note>original: "unsichtiges Feuer." A common concept in 17th-century Christian alchemy and mysticism, suggesting a divine energy that sustains the physical world</note> that is in all things. For all things are a fire, because **GOD** is and is called a "consuming fire." Now, if someone dies in "death"—that is, in himself, or in the temporal and not in the eternal, like any other irrational beast—woe to him. If he dies a...

in the **LORD**—that is, in His Word, in His knowledge, in repentance and sorrow—then he is blessed.

**81.** What does it mean then to die in Hell, or in death? Of this the Scripture says: To perish and be ruined in temporal pleasures, which is to fry and roast in hellish pitch <note>The author uses "Peche" (pitch/tar), a common medieval and early modern image of the sticky, burning substance of hell.</note>. This happens when we frequently overfill and overload ourselves with the good gifts of God, weighing down our hearts and eating and drinking ourselves to death upon them, as the world now does in every corner. They do not wish to live soberly or moderately at all, but rather in total gluttony <term>Vollbrätigkeit: an archaic term for being constantly "stuffed" or over-satiated</term>, never becoming sober, never becoming hungry, and never rightly thanking God. Because of this, we completely forget God and His Bread of Heaven, and never think upon the food of angels <note>original: "Speise der Engel," likely referring to the Manna or the Eucharist as spiritual sustenance</note>, without which we can neither maintain nor inherit eternal life. Thus, we are our own murderers in both body and soul, so that the Scripture says not without reason: That more perish through intemperance <term>Unmäßigkeit: a lack of moderation, specifically in eating and drinking</term> than by the sword. It is truly a great pity that almost no one on earth wishes to consider this. But whatever a person lives in and takes their pleasure in here, in that same thing they must also live there eternally. Whoever despises the good will of God here and does not live within it will be deprived of it there as well. Therefore, O dear man, let this be your primary concern, and consider how, and in what way, you may die and fall asleep in the **LORD** and not in death. Otherwise, nothing else can follow but that you must choke and drown in your own blood; and where you do not daily wake, pray, and cry out to God, then the blood of Christ, which you ignorantly eat and drink daily <note>This is a sharp warning regarding the Sacrament of the Altar (Communion); the author suggests that taking the blood of Christ without a wakeful, repentant heart leads to spiritual judgment rather than life</note>, is your death and chokes you. Believe it or leave it.

**82.** However, so that a person may know how to rightly protect themselves against all the fiery arrows of the Hellish Enemy, it is necessary that we, with all diligence, deeply and well take to heart and consider what the multitude of our grim and poisonous enemies might be, from whom David desired to be protected when he said: *Deliver me, O **LORD**, from my enemies, for I have taken my refuge in You. Look upon my enemies, for they are so many and they hate me out of malice. **LORD**, how very many are those who persecute me, how many rise up against me,* **Psalm 3, 25, 143.** <note>The author combines several Petitions from the Psalms of David to emphasize the soul's vulnerability</note>. This is so that we might know how to guard ourselves against them and not, out of ignorance, mistake the enemy for a friend. Our path that we are to walk toward heaven is not an open, paved road, but a secret, hidden, unknown path through a narrow gate—namely, within the person, internally in the spirit and not from the outside. Therefore, Christ directs us there and says: *Behold, the Kingdom of God is within you.* **Luke 17.** By this, He has given us to understand that we should remain alone in the inner heaven and seek God, and not wander on the outside; for what is outside of us does not concern us, **2 Corinthians 5:6.**

**83.** From this it follows that everything that is outside of us is our enemy, laid as a snare for us to catch us therein, just as David complains of this and says: *On the path they set an offense for me,* **Psalm 140.** Now, whoever separates Jesus and the visible and—

<meta>This page continues the Eighth Meditation, moving from the danger of worldly excess to the necessity of finding God within the soul rather than in the external, physical world. It emphasizes that the true "Heaven" where Christ dwells is the internal spirit of the believer.</meta>

### Eighth Spiritual [Meditation]

Whoever separates the invisible from one another and wishes to contemplate each separately—and does not seek both together in one, seeking the invisible within the visible, but rather outside of it—wanders far and is deceived. For whoever seeks **God** from the outside alone in the visible heaven, and not simultaneously in the inner, invisible heaven within his own person, should know that he will neither find nor encounter Him in the external. For He has ascended into heaven and hidden Himself in the Right Hand of **God** <note>original: "Gerechte GOttes." This refers to the *Dextera Dei*, the "Right Hand of God," symbolizing His power and presence which, the author argues, is located within the believer’s heart.</note>; there He sits to judge the living and the dead—namely, in the inner, invisible heaven within you, which you cannot see, and not in the external heaven which you see with your eyes. Or rather, whoever does not seek both together in one, but separates the external and the internal from each other, is not on the right narrow path but on the broad road. For this reason, David rejects everything external, empty, and separated as if it were tasteless salt, and says: *Blessed is the man who sets the name of the Lord as his hope, and does not look upon the proud, nor those who turn aside to lies.* (Psalm 40). For it is surely true: the greater the appearance and holiness presented to our eyes, the greater the deceit and guile we must fear behind it. This is because **God** leads His own people secretly and not publicly, so that the glory remains His alone, according to the Scripture: *He will not cry out or shout, and His voice will not be heard in the streets.* (Isaiah 42:2). For the true **Christ**, He has no form or beauty that would have pleased us.

**84.** Therefore, let no one think that he may comfort himself with an external **God** outside of him. Rather, you must comfort yourself with the Internal One who is within you—whom you do not need to run far after or seek elsewhere, for He is in you and with you. You must hold fast to Him, and by no means to that which is outside you. For thus speaks the true, only, living **God** in His own person: *Beside me there is no God or Savior.* (Isaiah 43, 45). Therefore, everything that is outside of you is of no use to you, but is more harmful than beneficial, unless you use it with great caution in the fear of **God**. Indeed, it is placed before you as a snare and a stone of stumbling, so that even daily necessities <term>Nohtdurfft: the basic requirements for survival, such as food and clothing</term> cannot be taken without "poison" and great danger. Therefore David prays: *My soul lies in the dust; make me alive according to your word.* (Psalm 119:25). For **God** has placed us in the midst of our enemies so that He may test us there: do we love the light more than the darkness? He does this so He might see how dear He is to us, or whether we wish to remain constant with Him and in Him. Therefore, every Christian is bound to call upon **God** daily from the heart, that **God** might have mercy on him, especially while among his enemies.

# The Eleventh Contemplation.
## Concerning the Mystery of the Divine Sabbath.

<margin>91.</margin> Because **GOD** created heaven and earth in six days / and rested on the seventh day / we have lived since the creation in the seventh day / which is **GOD** Himself / that is / we live in the rest of **GOD** / in the Sabbath of **GOD** / where all things are already finished and made / except / that they shall henceforth be sanctified on this day / which is to say / recognized / proclaimed / contemplated and expanded. Therefore we should by no means begin or do anything else / than to proclaim the glory of **GOD** alone / and not our own glory. From this it appears / that all things were prepared / made / and perfectly finished beforehand / so that nothing new needs to be prepared further; man finds everything ready / therefore he should not presume to begin and make something anew / but rather take / choose / grasp / and eat what **GOD** has set before Him; For the command of **GOD** reads thus: <note>original: Deut. 30</note> Deuteronomy 30: Choose life for yourself / so that you and your seed may live. So do not let death be pleasing to you / but life alone / and use what is necessary <term>Nohtdurfft<gloss>basic necessities of life, as opposed to luxury or excess</gloss></term> in all things / and by no means anything superfluous / (for necessity is life) and all this in the fear of **GOD** / that is / according to the will and command of **GOD**. Without the fear of **GOD** you shall touch nothing / for we are bound to ask the mouth of **GOD** / which is the fear of **GOD** / for counsel and to call upon Him in all things. We should live moderately and soberly at all times / and not <term>gorge and swill<gloss>original: fressen und sauffen; strong terms often used for animalistic consumption</gloss></term> ourselves to death / but apply diligence / to die with Christ on His cross. For man along with the whole creature / that is / the body of man / and the body of all things is the body of Christ / and that very cross / which Christ carries / upon which He / as the only Son of **GOD** (outside of whom there is no other **GOD**) stands outstretched / and suffers death / and redeems the creature.

<margin>92.</margin> The Eternal is otherwise nowhere to be found and encountered than in the Temporal / in which it has hidden and concealed itself / in that it can and must be grasped / and not otherwise outside of it; That is an unknown and wondrous and unbelievable thing to the world. And therefore the Outer and Inner / because of this combination / are no longer two to the true Christian / but One / united and not separated; Therefore one is now the other / the Old is the New / and the New is the Old / the Temporal is the Eternal / and the Eternal is the Temporal / and there is no further distinction. The Law is the Gospel / and the Gospel is the Law / the prophets are apostles / and the apostles are prophets / this witnesses...

## The Fourteenth Contemplation.

### THE MYSTERY AND SYMBOL OF THE HOLY TRINITY.
<note>original Latin: "S. S. TRINITATIS MYSTERIUM ET SYMBOLUM."</note>

### The Image and Mystery of the Holy Tri-Unity.

27. When man or the **Son of Man** is mentioned in the Holy Scripture, the perfect **Heavenly Man** is always understood to be within the visible and **Earthly Man**. However, by "God" and the "Name of God," <note>The OCR reads "Rahmen" (frame), but contextually and traditionally this is "Namen" (Name).</note> is understood the one true Divine Essence in three persons, in which the Father, the Word, and the Spirit are one, and not two, nor separated, divided, or contrary, but united: just as the Spirit, the water, and the blood are here on earth together as one and into one. For these three things are, in a Divine person <note>The text uses "Göttlichen Menschen" (Divine Man), referring to the archetype of humanity.</note> in the innermost foundation, **One** and not **Three**; united and not separated, neither from within nor from without. Instead, they together constitute a perfect human being. appears in the body visibly, tangibly, and perceptibly, as the Prophet says: *He who alone lives in the Body.* <note>original Latin: "Qui solus in Corpore vivit."</note> And how can he be considered a perfect human being who does not know what those three are? But where these three things are not perfectly together—even if the form or shape of a human were present—it is still not a perfect human being, but is to be reckoned only as a dumb beast, and an earthly, mortal man.

98. Now, where a perfect human is to exist, not only must the soul and the body be together—that is, not only the Word or temporal life within the body—but above all things, the third must be present, which makes these two things into a perfect Heavenly human; otherwise, he remains merely a beast. Namely, to these two must be added the Spirit of God, or Heavenly Understanding, which governs and restrains the human soul, Word, or life. For where this is lacking and does not exist, everything is still false, empty, and dead, and is not to be regarded as a true, perfect human being. For the Spirit and the Word are the Heavenly Marriage of God, which we must have together if we wish to be perfect Heavenly humans. It is not enough that we have the Word; we must also have the Spirit, who awakens the Word and makes it living and active within us. For the Scripture testifies that the Spirit of God is not in all people, saying: *The Spirit blows where He wills,* John 3. *Faith is not of all,* 2 Thess. 3. *They do not all have the knowledge,* 1 Cor. 8. *They have not all obeyed the Gospel,* Rom. 10. These alone belong to God who are born of the Word of promise and are driven by the Spirit of God, Rom. 8, 9. Therefore, where the Word, the soul, the bride, and the outer life are, there the Spirit—as the King, Bridegroom, and Regent—must also be; otherwise, he cannot be reckoned as a perfect, heavenly, whole human being. For if the Word, or the temporal outer life, wishes to be healthy, it must have its protection, its support, and its lap in which to rest and dwell. Otherwise, where it does not stand in the Spirit of God but in itself, it must perish and come to nothing; it eats itself away and consumes itself, for without the Spirit of God it cannot exist or endure at all. But where the Spirit and the Word are together without the body, they are solely Heavenly and not earthly; there they are also beyond our reach. Therefore, these two must have their third, namely the body, where they are to work; for outside of the body there is no activity. For the Majesty of God has ordered it so wonderfully that the body is dead without these two, and these two are nothing without a body, and cannot be sensed, grasped, or understood.

99. Therefore, because these two are combined and placed and bound inseparably into one marriage, it is impossible for one to exist or endure in the body as whole and perfect without the other, unless they sleep together in one bed. For an unbelieving wife is sanctified by a believing husband, according to 1 Cor. 7. belongs together, one and not two; according to the Scripture: The Word became flesh and dwells in us. John 1. ## The Fifteenth Meditation.
### CONCERNING THE CIRCUMCISION OF CHRIST <note>original: "DE CIRCUMCISIONE CHRISTI"</note>
## On the Circumcision of Christ, and how man becomes, is, and remains an image of God.

<margin>106.</margin> *I have come to send a fire on earth, and how I wish it were already burning!* <note>original: "Luc. 12"</note> Here, Almighty God! Who among us would rightly consider these wonderful words of Christ, and why they are there? For truly I say to you, they are not spoken in vain or for nothing, but they carry something important within them and reveal to us the great and mighty wonders and mysteries of God. For they testify to us and indicate that man is a wonderful, living image of the invisible, living God: namely, that man is a fire, and must live in the fire and through the fire. For all things are a fire, and this fire is in man, and is man himself; for man is the **Heavenly Phoenix**. <note>The Phoenix is a mythical bird that burns and is reborn from its own ashes; here it symbolizes the soul being purified and renewed by God's spiritual fire</note> And this is because God is all things, and all things are God, who is a **consuming fire**. <note>A common biblical description of God's holiness and power, found in Hebrews 12:29</note> Therefore, man should be like God and be what He is, as an image of God and a son of the Most High. And he is indeed that, but only within, and not outside of God. Now, whichever man lives and stands in God, to him all things are a heavenly fire—that is: a light and a lamp, as well as a cool cloud and a lovely sunshine, and the grace of God itself. And such a man is exactly that—to himself and to others as well—and while still in his living body, wherever he stands and goes, he is in heaven and in **Paradise**. But whoever turns away from God and lives and stands in himself, and not in God, he...

# Meditation.
DDD 4

...unconverted man is indeed also a fire, but not a heavenly one; rather, he is an earthly and hellish fire, a darkness, and the wrath of God itself, which breaks all things apart, crushes them, devours them, and consumes them. And such is exactly what that person becomes, primarily to himself and subsequently to others as well; for while still in his living body, wherever he stands or walks, he is in the abyss of hell, and all his food is nothing but hellish pitch.

<margin>107.</margin> For the one and only eternal Man, C. J. <note>Christ Jesus</note>, is the two-edged sword that goes out of the mouth of God. He is Heaven, and He is also Hell; He is the water and the fire; He is death and life; He is the light and the darkness; He is the day and the night; and He is God, all in all. This is at once very comforting and also very terrifying, according to the Scripture: *It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.* <note>original: "Hebr. 10"</note> It is comforting to the godly, but terrifying to the wicked; for to the godly, all things are good, but to the wicked, all things are evil and impure. However, that things are and become evil within a person, and undergo such a transformation, happens because those things are taken out of the hand of God. That is, when something comes to exist outside of God within a person—whether it stands in his own hand, or proceeds from him, or is done or spoken by him—it is already nothingness and death. This is not God’s fault, but the fault of the person; for man should stand in God, and rest and work in Him alone. This is the true Sabbath, according to the Scripture: *Early in the morning I will prepare myself for You and look up.* <note>original: "Ps. 5"</note> This occurs when God works in us and we stand idle <note>Meaning a state of spiritual stillness or "Gelassenheit," where the human will is quiet so God can act</note>. For when man no longer rests in God, and loses sight of Him, wanting to be more and wiser than God, he falls into the abyss of hell, into the outermost darkness. Then, because of the separation from the inner [divine] being, it becomes a dire necessity and an infirmity <term>Gebresten: a spiritual defect or ailment</term>; for that which should remain at rest and remain hidden breaks forth and allows itself to be seen in action. Thus, what we ought to have and possess in God as something good, invisible, and unknowable becomes visible and recognizable within us as something evil. For all things, in man as well as in God, should be and remain One and good, harming no one but benefiting everyone, according to the Scripture: *Salvation from our enemies.* <note>original: "Salutem ex Inimicis nostris"; likely referring to Luke 1:71</note> For salvation must also come to us and be born out of our enemies. But when we transgress the commandment of God and appropriate for ourselves what is God's—presuming to possess it outside of Him when it is by no means ours, but God's—it immediately becomes sin, evil, and an abomination within us, apart from God. Therefore the Scripture says: *I was silent and did not open my mouth, etc.* <note>original: "Obmutui & non aperui &c."; Psalm 39:9. The author suggests a quiet yielding to God's will.</note> And thus we force God to do evil; for He does the good willingly of Himself within us, but He does the evil only through our own will within us, unwillingly. However, because man is a son of God, he should have and possess all things in God, and by no means outside of Him; for in God, he is a lord and a king over all things. Outside of God, however, he is not only empty, naked, and bare, but also entirely nothing and dead; for then all things rule over him, and all things are against him.

<margin>108.</margin> Therefore, man should stand in God at every moment and before His countenance, as an empty, dead vessel that is nothing...

[Man] has nothing / nor can he do anything that is his own / but everything is God's / and for that reason he should pray to God / that He would feed / satisfy / and fill / ignite / and make him alive with His power / with His light / and with His heavenly fire from above. 109. When God speaks in us and out of us / that is our song / our vow, and our oath / which God loves and which well pleases Him; if not / then the opposite is within us. For when he boasts and reflects himself outside of God / that is / in himself / and in his own deeds / then he falls into **pride** <note>original: "Hoffart"; meaning sinful arrogance or vanity.</note> / and becomes a hideous **devil's mask** <note>original: "Teuffelslarven"; 'Larve' traditionally meant a mask or a frightening specter.</note> / shaming and blaspheming God in all things. Thus man must overcome the world and all things / and be an immovable rock to all things / and cut and separate himself from all things / both from within and from without / and [be] alone in [God].

# The Sixteenth Meditation.
## On the Sunday of Epiphany.

<margin>110.</margin> All things are one, and one is all things, and all things are in all things; and this is because there is no more than one single God in heaven and on earth. In the inner ground, this is as much as to say: God and man are one **CHRIST**, and not two; united and not separated. But as to how all things are two, and divided, it is thus: 1. Firstly, the outer, earthly man knows nothing at all of this unity; he does not understand it without God. 2. And secondly, he does not wish to believe it. Therefore, all things are "two" to him, and he considers them as two, for he does not understand the **birth of God**, the **covenant of God**, or the **testament of God**, by which God has united and bound Himself with man. That is to say, he does not believe that the Eternal is to be sought and found in the outer alone; therefore, he treats the outer as an empty thing. Thus, the man who misuses an Eternal thing is empty and dead; and all things are likewise empty and dead to him. He does not know that all things are a **fire of God**, that is, a living, consuming fire, and the eternal **Phoenix** <note>The Phoenix is used here as a mystical symbol for Christ or the soul being reborn through the "fire" of divine love and purification.</note> itself, who lives in the fire and is to be sought and found in the fire alone. Therefore, man seeks the Eternal in that which he can never grasp, which is far above him, and does not know that it is so near to him, and that he is it himself; otherwise, he would learn to conduct himself quite differently in all things. For nothing is empty; rather, all things are filled with the **Majestic Presence**, the almighty light, and the living power of God. From this ignorance, it necessarily follows that all things must be spoken of in two ways; and thus that which is one in God becomes two in man. Therefore, all things are both the truth and the lie, according to how they are spoken and understood. In God, one; in man, two. In God, good; in man, evil.

# Sixteenth Spiritual [Contemplation] etc.

...heavenly light, toward the goal that God has set for them, and do not remain within the <term>boundary<note>original: "Termino." A Latin term for a limit or fixed point.</note></term> that God has established for them, but rather overstep it; and in that overstepping, death is at the door.

He should not hallow or exalt himself, but God alone, so that God finds His rest in him. He should also not meddle in foreign matters, nor judge or condemn anything, nor try to be clever or play the master; for all things have been contained in the judgment of God from eternity, and there is nothing new under the sun upon the earth. No one remembers what happened before; likewise, what happens afterward will not be remembered by those who come after, Ecclesiastes 1. They shall proclaim the Lord to the children’s children. They shall come and preach His righteousness to a people yet to be born, that He has done it, Psalm 22. Therefore, man can do nothing better than to believe and <term>consent<note>original: "consentiren."</note></term> to the Word of God in all things, and await its fulfillment within him, according to the Scripture, John 4: The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way and found it to be so. *O good will, how much do you provide? How wonderful are the works you perform?* <note>original: "O bona voluntas, quanta præstas? quam admiranda operaris?"</note>

### A.
## The First Part: Concerning GOD.

### I. Of His Essence.

<margin>1.</margin> GOD alone is the good tree: and all men are rotten trees. God is Humility and Simplicity; the Devil is Pride and Ignorance.

<margin>2.</margin> All things are God to me; as long as I accept all things as being sent to me by God, I find God in all things.

<margin>3.</margin> Everything I see and do not see is GOD to me: for by His wisdom, GOD has created all things. In all things, one sees His wisdom. And thus, God is everything in all things.

<margin>4.</margin> God is Nothing, neither This nor That, and yet He is Everything: no one can say what God is. <note>This refers to "apophatic theology," the idea that God is so far beyond human understanding that He can only be described by what He is not.</note>

<margin>5.</margin> The distinction of the Persons of the Trinity <note>original: "Differentia Personarum Trinitatis"</note> is only external to us; within us there is no difference, but all are One.

<margin>6.</margin> Scripture is God: Nature is God: Man is God: thus you have the three Persons of the One, Living, and True God. <note>original: "Scriptura Deus est : Natura Deus est : Homo Deus est : sic habes tres Personas Unius, Vivi, Veri Dei." This is a radical mystical statement suggesting that the divine manifests through the Word, the physical world, and humanity itself.</note>

<margin>7.</margin> The One, who is smaller than all things, contains, exceeds, and penetrates them. All things are full of God: the Lord fills every single place. <note>original: "Continet, exsuperat, penetrat minor omnibus Unus. Omnia plena Dei : Dominus Loca singula complet."</note>

<margin>8.</margin> To not know God is a most wretched thing; but to have known Him is the highest happiness. This flows from the contemplation of the World—both the greater macrocosm and the microcosm <note>The "microcosm" refers to man as a small-scale reflection of the entire universe.</note>.

<margin>9.</margin> The sacred breath blows from afar where it pleases, breathing the heavenly Ternary <note>the Trinity</note> of the Almighty. It ignites the tiny spark of the Secret Tinder. Grant this to us, O Holy Trinity; let it illuminate our innermost hearts with the True Light, we who are thrice dedicated to you by the holy, sacred, and hidden Word. <note>original: "Flamen sacratum... Fomitis Secreti... Vero Lumine..."</note>

---

### II. Of God’s Name.

<margin>1.</margin><margin>even he may be an image of God, not of Grace, but of the Wrath of God.</margin> God’s Name is Everything, or all things: that is, all things bear the image of God, Hebrews 1:3. So much so that even the Devil

<margin>2.</margin> Since the name of God is in all things and in all creatures (as indeed He is), it follows that whoever misuses even the least of these misuses the name of God—which is a terrifying thing and should be greatly feared.

<margin>3.</margin> There is but one Name in heaven and on earth to which alone all honor is due and should be shown, and not to the visible creatures, which are only the images and shadows of that Name. For all other names exist and come out of that one—that is, from GOD—and all their power, effect, and essence is from God, and flows out from Him, and back into Him again. Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but to your Name give glory: for your Mercy and your Virtue. <note>original: "Non ergo nobis, Domine... sed Nomini tuo da gloriam..."</note>

<margin>4.</margin> The Name of the Lord is "That" <note>original: "Id"</note> in which God has revealed himself to us.

<margin>5.</margin> There is no more in heaven and on earth than one single God, according to the Word: You shall have no other gods. <note>original: "Non habebis Deos alienos."</note> There is

There is also no more than a single, threefold Name of GOD in heaven and on earth. This Name of God is all things: and it is He who is our help and shield: whom we are obligated to call upon, according to the Scripture: <note>original: "Quicunque invocaverit Nomen Domini, salvus erit"</note> **Whoever shall call upon the Name of the Lord shall be saved.** This is as much as to say: This single eternal God has divided Himself into a threefold Name, or into a threefold Word, which is the "What" <note>The essence or substance of being.</note>. ### III. Concerning God's Word.

1. **E**very Word is Threefold: <note>original: "Omne Verbum Trinum"</note> GOD the One-in-Three <note>original: "Uni-Trinus"</note> revealed Himself through the Word: for in every Word the most Holy TRINITY lies hidden and shines forth. **V. V. S.**

2. If we knew or considered who or what the Word is that speaks within us, we would surely not be so thoughtless and frivolous with our words, but would rather save the useless talk and leave it aside.

<margin>1 John 4</margin> 3. <note>original: "Qui confitetur Jesum, &c."</note> **Whoever confesses Jesus, etc.** Whoever holds it as certain in his heart and believes without doubt that the Word of God is the living, <term>salvific power</term> <note>original: "Seligmachende Kraft," referring to the power that brings about salvation or spiritual bliss.</note> of God, and seals that in his heart, remembering it every hour, and places all his comfort and confidence upon it in all needs—he carries GOD with him in his heart: That is, God remains in him, and he in God.

4. <note>original: "Non ex solo Pane, &c ex T. P."</note> **Not by bread alone, etc.** A person may live on any kind of food alone, such as bread alone, fish alone, meat alone, or herbs alone, etc. Just so, one can live by the Word of GOD alone, without any of the others. For all things are made out of the Word of God: Psalm 33:6. Just as all seeds become a body, so also does the Word of God: For it is the true <term>primal seed</term> <note>original: "Haupt-Saamen," literally "head-seed" or the principal/original seed from which others spring.</note> of all seeds. For many people do not have the necessary food, so that they cannot sustain themselves by means of food—so unequal are the stomachs of men, both the poor and the rich. Now, every stomach requires its "weight" <note>A specific amount or measure of nourishment.</note>; it cannot have less. But for those who do not have the weight to give to the stomach, the Word of God compensates for it: and their mouth does not know it, their eyes do not see it. Thus, one often eats two pounds but chews only one or a half. For God is wonderful in His works.

<margin>1 John 4</margin> 5. <note>original: "Quod Jesus sit Christus"</note> **That Jesus is the Christ.** That the incorruptible seed of the Word of God is our salvation and **Heavenly Food**, through which the New Body is sustained for eternal life.

6. We have one single Word: and in that Word, and from—

2. <note>original: "Noli altum sapere"</note> **Do not be high-minded**: Do not let these thoughts enter your heart, as if you understood the Scripture: Nor interpret it according to your own opinion, for in doing so you exalt yourself against God, who is an incomprehensible light. # VI. On the Law and the Gospel.

1. <term>True Theological Magic</term> <note>original: "Theologia vera Mageja"; here "Magic" refers to the divine, creative power of God's wisdom.</note>, is when Christ is adored upon the Triple Cross.

2. *Law & Gospel are one and the same. He who separates the law of God from the Gospel, dissolves Christ: for the Gospel is Law.* <note>original: "Lex & Euangelium unum & idem. Qui legem Dei separat ab Euangelio, solvit Christum: Euangelium enim Lex est."</note>

3. Our academics carry great titles / writing themselves as *Doctors & Masters of Theology, & yet they are ignorant of what Theology is?* <note>original: "Doctores & Magistros Theologiæ, & ignorant quid sit Theologia?"</note> For <term>Theology</term> is humility / <term>Repentance</term> <note>original: "Pœnitentia"</note>, Christ. What is the <term>Universal Gospel</term>? Here let him be silent / who can be silent / and let the highly learned Doctors here give counsel; what does it matter if they do not know it? What kind of fine Doctors are they then? Because they do not know it / I must tell it to them: It consists of the seven letters <term>Wellari</term> <note>A mystical term often associated with the seven planetary spirits or the unfolding of creation.</note>. That is seven days: Or the seventh day itself.

*For in six days God created Heaven & Earth, and on the Seventh He rested.* <note>original: "Sex enim diebus creavit Deus Cœlum & Terram, Septimo requievit."</note> And though you do not know it / it is nonetheless right and good / and so it shall be.

# The Second Part: Of Christ.

## I. Of Christ’s Incarnation.

<margin>a.</margin> 1. <note>original: "Qui ſolvit Jeſum, id eſt, qui negat eum veniſſe in Carne & Carnem noſtram aſſumpſiſſe, hic eſt, Antichriſtus & mendax"</note> He who dissolves Jesus—that is, he who denies that He has come in the Flesh and has assumed our Flesh—this person is the Antichrist and a liar: for He brought us His own Flesh, which is Celestial and heavenly Flesh: but our flesh is from the Earth, unclean, foul, and mortal. <note>original: "Ego autem Vermis & non-Homo"</note> I, however, am a Worm and no man. <note>original: "Homo Putredo, & Filius Hominis Vermis"</note> Man is Rot, and the Son of Man a Worm. Job 25. The little worm of Jacob.

2. <note>original: "Qui non habet Filium Dei, Vitam non habet"</note> He who does not have the Son of God does not have Life: That is / he who does not believe / that He is God's Son / and that GOD is His Father / he does not have life / but rather he still remains stuck in death.

3. <note>original: "Chriſtus naturam humanam aſſumpſit (Formam) non Carnem Corruptam"</note> Christ assumed human nature (the Form), not Corrupt Flesh: For this [corrupt flesh] is not without stain and filth; whoever is ignorant of this cannot arrive at the true knowledge of God.

4. The world neither knows / nor believes / that God is Man (<note>original: "J. C. in Carne veniſſe"</note> that Jesus Christ has come in the Flesh, 1 John 4:2) / but only affirms that He is Spirit; from this, all error arises.

## II. Of the Suffering of Christ.

1. <note>original: "Chriſtus patitur in omnibus Creaturis: quia omnes Creaturæ filius Dei"</note> Christ suffers in all Creatures: because all Creatures [are in] the Son of God. <note>The author suggests a mystical union where Christ's presence permeates all of creation, meaning any harm to nature is felt by Christ.</note>

2. All creatures suffer in Christ / and Christ suffers in them: <note>original: "Siquo abuteris, Chriſtum denuò Crucifigis"</note> If you abuse any creature, you crucify Christ anew.

3. <note>original: "Qui deſcendunt in Mare, &c."</note> "Those who go down to the sea," etc. Psalm 106. The Interpreter <note>likely a specific theological commentator</note> seems to say this to me: In the entire Machine of the World, and in all Creatures, Christ suffers, from the Beginning of the World until the end. This drives us altogether into the Fear of GOD / and hallows the right use of all creatures and condemns their abuse.

4. Christ wanders about naked and very poor: Not clothed in purple but in a lowly state <note>original: "abſurdus" — meaning out of place or disregarded by the world</note>, with torn clothing: Because of this, He is not known by everyone, but only by a few. You will indeed be blessed if you sufficiently understand the veil of the poor man, and clothe yourself with it. Poverty itself is Christ the SON of the highest GOD: Love this, adore this: Revere the Cross continually: This will bless you exceedingly into eternal Ages.

If you now are a child of God / then you must also be in that and be found in that which is your Father's. <note>original: "Spiritus enim reddit Spiritui noſtro teſtimonium, quòd ſimus filii DEI"</note> For the Spirit bears witness to our spirit that we are children of GOD.
