## IV. Of the Sacraments.

1. We human beings are all the innkeeper / to whom the Samaritan entrusted the care of his sick / and left us 2 groschen <note>original: "Groschen" — a silver coin. This refers to the Parable of the Good Samaritan in Luke 10, where the "two pence" are interpreted here as the two sacraments.</note> for this purpose; these are now 2 *Local Sacraments* <note>original: "Sacramenta Localia"</note>, namely the body and blood of Christ: that is Baptism and the Lord's Supper: which are not external sacraments, but internal ones. If we spend more than this, He will repay us when He returns: This shall be our profit and our reward: This also has a *double sense, for both good and evil.* <note>original: "Duplicem Sensum, tam in Bonum, quàm in Malum."</note> We are the steward / to whom the household is entrusted / for which we must give an account to God. We are also the debtor and the servant / to whom the Lord entrusted the 5 pounds with which to trade. <note>Refers to the Parable of the Talents or Minas in Luke 19.</note> The grace of God in us / which we make use of / that is our increase and our profit.

2. *Through external sacraments we are saved, so that the outer confirms the inner.* <note>original: "Per Exteriora Sacramenta salvamur, ut Exterius confirmet Interiùs."</note>

## V. Of Holy Baptism.

Going to Baptism and to the sacrament / is in itself nothing and entirely in vain and for naught / if it does not happen in faith and out of faith / that is / in the spirit / and in God. You boast greatly and rely upon your baptism / and yet you do not have faith / and do not know what baptism is. You should and must know / that faith and baptism are one / and not two. Faith is the baptism / and baptism is the faith. Baptism is a work / but faith is a word: Now word and work must agree / and not be separated / so that one is this / and the other is that / but both must be one and united. If you are now rightly baptized / that is / if you are baptized by Christ and not by priests <note>The original uses "Pfaffen," a term that by this period often carried a derogatory tone toward institutional clergy, emphasizing spiritual baptism over the mere ritual performed by men.</note> alone: then your baptism must be faith and must become faith: And faith in itself must be a baptism / with which GOD baptizes you for eternal life: otherwise it does not help you / even if you are baptized by men: For / without the baptism of Christ you remain eternally entangled and bound in the snares of the devil. The faith / which is the baptism / the baptism which is Christ / Christ who is the Son of God / the Son of God who is the eternal truth / the truth which is the Word of God / the Word that is GOD Himself / is our redemption / namely the blood of Jesus Christ. And if the truth / that is / the blood of Christ does not make us free / then we cannot be redeemed. And even if the priest baptized you ten times / it is still all a wasted effort and labor / without GOD.

## The Third Part: Concerning Man.

### I. Concerning Faith.

1. Our faith has its certain limits by which it is enclosed, and which one must not cross: namely, the Mercy of God <note>original Latin: "Fides nostra habet certos suos Terminos... scilicet Misericordiam Dei"</note>; according to that passage of Scripture: *I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy* <note>Exodus 33:19; Romans 9:15</note>: as if to say: If anyone recognizes me as Merciful and has sought mercy from me, I will have mercy on him; but he who does not do so, in what way shall I have mercy on him? I draw no one against their will, but only the willing: for our will is the "drawing" <note>An allusion to John 6:44, "No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him."</note> of our Heavenly Father. (God in Man always wills the Good, but the Devil always twists it toward the Evil.)

2. *Blessed is he who is not offended in Me.* <note>original Latin: "Beatus, qui non fuerit scandalizatus in Me." See Matthew 11:6.</note>
He who is ashamed of God and His Word, or is offended by it, of him He shall be ashamed in turn at the time when he will have the greatest need of Him.

3. In God alone. Everything that does not happen out of faith is sin <note>Romans 14:23</note>; that is: Everything that does not happen out of God’s Word (which is the basis of faith) and is done or undertaken, that is sin.

### II. Concerning Prayer.

1. When we wish to worship God rightly, we must worship all three Persons in one God.

2. Meditation on the Word is the very invocation of God. <note>original Latin: "Verbi meditatio, est ipsissima Dei Invocatio." This suggests that deeply reflecting on scripture is itself a form of prayer.</note>

3. Man should thoroughly know that he, as he is in himself, has absolutely nothing: but if he desires to have and possess anything of Eternal Goods, he must first ask for them from God with the greatest diligence. God gives nothing to the one who does not ask, unless he is in great earnest: without asking, one has nothing. God alone must and can give it. No one has it of himself, nor can he receive it from another person, for that person has just as little, and is just as poor, as he is.

4. Not praying is the greatest sin. Our strength and armor consist only in this: that we recognize our inability and utterly despair of our own power, [seeking] alone God’s help and assistance...

### IV. On the Christian Life.

1. Consider, O human, who you are? Curse no one, despise no one, mock or laugh at no one. Do not anger, harm, nor offend anyone, whether they be great or small, young or old, poor or rich, lame or healthy (God has created them both), as dearly as you love God in heaven. Why? Because God has hidden Himself in every person, in the evil as well as in the pious. And the Word that is in man is the greatest wonder above all wonders, of great power. Therefore, guard yourself so that you do not violate the high majesty of God. For everything in heaven and on earth belongs to God, the pious as well as the evil. Now, if someone does you good, accept it with joy and thank God for it, for it comes from God through the person, whether they be good or evil. If someone offends you, do not grumble; not a single hair can be bent without the will of God. Do not avenge yourself in any way, but bear it with patience and give God the glory: for in this way you fulfill the will of God. Rather, pray to God that He might enlighten the offender and have mercy on us all. For Christ also prayed thus on the Cross for us all:

> Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

And in summary, what you do not want others to do to you, that you should also not do to them; and what you would like for yourself, do also for others. If you see someone committing something evil or unseemly, sigh to God, and if the opportunity arises, rebuke the evil with a gentle heart, with deep humility and modesty. If they accept it, well and good, then thank God; if not, then let God rule.

### VI. Gelassenheit <term>Gelassenheit: a central term in German mysticism and Pietism, meaning "yieldedness," "serenity," or the total surrender of one's own will to God</term>.

As long as we do not cast off our hope in ourselves, in our flesh and blood, or in our own doing and ceasing, powers and abilities—and indeed, also our hope and fear in everything that appears in this world to be visible, great, powerful, respectable, magnificent, terrifying, useful or useless, harmful or pious, helpful or hindering—in short, as long as we do not entirely and utterly forsake everything that we might desire in heaven and earth, and fear and honor only the true God who created all this: so long can we not rightly hold fast to the One, Eternal, Invisible Good, which is God himself, nor rightly act or walk with Him, much less be truly acceptable or pleasing to Him. > Sell all, and follow Me <note>original Latin: *Vende Omnia, & Me sequere*</note>.

The Clay <term>Leimen: literally 'glue' or 'loam,' referring here to the heavy, earthly materiality and the fallen state of humanity, often associated with the 'dust of the earth' from which Adam was formed</term> is not a dead Death, or a mere thing, but a living Death that stirs and fights against the Life that is God Himself. Now, sin and death, the devil and hell, are all one thing: from this it follows that all of these are the Clay. For David, while he was still in the Clay, lamented thus: "For in Death there is no one who remembers You; in Hell, who will give thanks to You?" <note>original Latin: *Quoniam non est in Morte, qui memor sit Tui: In Inferno autem quis confitebitur Tibi, Ps. 6.*</note>

These enemies mentioned above stand at once in the Clay, and are the Clay, which is the World. Since the devil, the Old Serpent, was cast out of heaven, Revelation 12:12, where else would he be but in the world? This is his and his companions' lodging, and our prison and hell: into which we were cast after the Fall because of sin. If he is now in the Great World, then he is also in the Little World, for these two both have one nature. Therefore Death and Life are hidden in all things, just as they are in man. **The last of the enemies to be destroyed is Death.** <note>original Latin: *Ultimus Inimicorum, destruetur Mors.*</note> Death, the Clay, the earthly body is the last enemy, which shall be melted in fire and destroyed on the Last Day: when God will create a New Heaven and other Earths, or bring to light that which already is now and from eternity, but still hidden in His Word; God will bring all of that to light. 

Here follows yet a much greater, more unspeakable miracle, which is beyond all human reason and cannot be sufficiently expressed. And it is this: What is all of this after all? And therefore, just as God is in all things and is all things Himself; so also are Death and Life in all things: Death is Life, and Life is Death, quite miraculously. # MISCELLANEA.
<note>Latin: "Miscellany" or a collection of various thoughts.</note>

## I. THE BINARY.
<note>original Latin: "Binarius". This refers to the concept of duality or pairs.</note>

All things are Two: because the Being of all things depends on unity: Two-faced Janus <note>The Roman god of beginnings, gates, and transitions, usually depicted with two faces looking in opposite directions.</note>. All things are Time and Eternity.
GOD is the Good / Life / All / Light / Justice / Heaven / etc.
Man is Evil / Death / Nothingness / Darkness / Sin / Hell / etc.
The Good is from eternity / uncreated; Evil was created by GOD / not so that it should be evil / but so that He might reveal His goodness through it / and make something good out of it.

## 2. CHARACTERS.
<note>original Latin: "Characteres". In this mystical context, it refers to both the letters of the alphabet and spiritual signs or seals.</note>

Either the letters of the alphabet are capsules, or receptacles and dwellings of spirits, in which the treasures of God lie hidden and enclosed. In herbs, words, etc.
If Word is joined to Word, Cross to Cross, and Body to Body—from these three joined together comes the Living Letter.

## 3. MAN.

Time is the Death of all things. Man is a small part of Time: therefore also a small part of death. Man, composed of Time and Eternity, is both Death and Life.

## 4. NOTHINGNESS.

We flow out FROM Nothingness; from Nothingness He made all things out of nothing <note>original Latin: "EX Nihilo fluimus, Nihilo Nihil Omnia fecit."</note>.
If you ask, what are men? Nothingness: God is everything.

### 7. ÆNIGMATA.
<note>Latin: "Riddles."</note>

1. There are three of you who are able to write
In three books, reason and senses.
Each writing and writer has
His own way, his alphabet, and place.
Yet in the end the hand of the Three
Is recognized as only one book and no more.

2. Help, GOD! What a wonder is this!
I saw a thing, and I know not what;
It was not dead, it did not live;
What might that be? Give me a report.
If you know this, it is my will:
Do not say it, yet keep it quietly with you.

3. Someone saw through a vision
Sun, moon, and star in a single light;
Now it is large, soon it is small;
What kind of wonder might that be?

4. **I** is **Chi**, and **Chi** is **I**; <note>"Chi" is the Greek letter Χ, the first letter of Christ (Χριστός). The riddle refers to the mystical union where the "I" of the believer becomes one with Christ.</note> the world does not know this secret and mystery, this bond <note>original Latin: "Copulam"</note> and union <note>original Latin: "Unionem"</note>, and does not want to believe it.

True Theology is Magic, therefore all things are magical.
What is true Magic? When Christ is worshipped on the Triple Cross.

## MAGIC (from MARY)
<note>original: "MAGIA (ex MARIA)." The author uses an anagrammatic wordplay between "Magia" (Magic/Wisdom) and "Maria" (Mary), suggesting that spiritual power is born from the same soul-state as the Mother of Christ.</note>

Christ the Magus, the magical offspring of the highest Magus,
Revealed only to the Wise, unknown to the unwise,
Newly born, he showed himself to the Magi and the Shepherds:
Who themselves were transformed and became true Magi.
All the utterances of the highest Magus are magical.
The Magus breathed forth the Divine Word <note>original: "Magejan," a mystical term for the creative breath or speech of God</note> out of the Magician’s Silence.
These things are known only to the Magi: hidden from the non-Magi.
The Magi shall hear "Come"; the non-Magi shall hear "Depart."
Here, the non-Magi trample the Magi, while the Magi care for nothing;
The Magi shall trample the non-Magi in the world to come.
You non-Magi, pray to the Magus, that he might lead you to become Magi,
Lest the highest Magus burn you, as condemned non-Magi.
<note>The term "Magus" (singular) and "Magi" (plural) here refers to the "Wise Men" of the Nativity but is used as a technical term for those with spiritual insight, contrasted with the "non-Magi" or the spiritually blind.</note>

# Postscript

and could collectively rejoice all at once. For it is deafened by the excessive clamor and the tedious, confused din of manifold tones and melodies.

2. In like manner appears the human condition—and among others, primarily Christendom at this time—when one considers the great multitude of teachers and guides, and the diversity of doctrine they give to man to attain his salvation, where each one shouts out his own, so that he may call many of his own to himself, and does not point to the only and inward Christ, the universal Savior, who is the only Word and the one voice of the eternal Father, through which He reveals Himself in life, power, and glory. And in Him all creatures in heaven and on earth are created; thus He alone is set as the Light, Leader, and Teacher, indeed as the Lord and Judge over all people.

3. What, however, has such conflicting shouting—using the same Name, saying "here is Christ, there is Christ, come here, come there"—achieved until now? That is as clear as day: the fruits reveal it. The times teach and write it inside and out. The signs show it in all kingdoms, lands, cities, and houses, through war, bloodshed <note>original: "Blutstürzung," literally a plunging or shedding of blood</note>, injustice, violence, raging, cunning, and lies; indeed, in countless forms of godlessness and falsehood in all governments and estates, in the actions and essence of men. So much so, that instead of the praise of God, where every breath should praise the Lord, now the heaven and the earth are filled with the sighing of Christ and of all creatures with Him, over the accumulated misery, anguish, great need, and countless heartache that springs from such confused shouting.

4. In truth! Where else but in Christ’s power and office alone is it to make the blind see, the deaf hear, the lame walk, the lepers clean, to heal all sicknesses, to cast out evil spirits, and to wake the dead through His own unique Word and voice? "I will do it," Matthew 8:3. "Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened," Matthew 11:28. Thus, everything that is not He Himself, and not with Him or sent by Him, cannot fail to be His adversary and scatterer, and therefore drives a contrary effect: to make the seeing blind, the hearing deaf, the walking lame, the clean leprous, to make men into incarnate devils and children of hell, and to kill the living.

5. Alas! The great distress of this time! Who then recognizes the day of tribulations and the hour of temptation, when everything stands confused and perverted? Christ must be called Beelzebub <note>A name for the devil; the author is referencing Matthew 10:25, where Christ warns that if the master of the house is called a demon, so will his followers be</note>; Lucifer calls himself Christ. The Divine Word of hidden wisdom must be a heresy, a fantasy <note>original: "Phantasey," here meaning a deluded imagination or false invention</note>, and an error; abomination, superstition, lies, and blasphemy are now called "Theology." In short, because everything evil comes in the name of the Lord and through prayer, the Devil now sits upon the throne, and Christ, with His precious blood, is trampled underfoot and daily rooted out.

6. This appears unbelievable and grizzly to the world, because it hears nothing else but shouting about Christ and His Word,

# Postscript

6. She speaks of faith, of religion, of prayer, of good works; she observes Baptism and the Lord’s Supper. But she neither sees, nor hears, nor recognizes that she is blinded by outward, vanishing appearances. Her ears are deafened by the excessive shouting of the "buyers and sellers" <note>A reference to the money-changers Christ drove from the Temple, here symbolizing those who profit from religion</note>, stuffed with countless false books and papers, and her heart and spirit are shattered by deceptive teaching. Therefore, she cannot distinguish between light or darkness, truth or lies, nor can she discern the prophecy now being fulfilled, even though she is struck, humbled, and convicted by all its signs.

7. Truly, this great spiritual distress <note>original: "Seelen-noht," meaning soul-need or an internal spiritual crisis</note> should go to our hearts and drive us to pay earnest attention to the words of Christ and his prophecy and warning, where He says: *Many will come in my name and deceive even the chosen, and yet few will be those who find the narrow way and inherit salvation.*

8. But the time is already arriving; its end is here—the earnest trial by fire <note>original: "Prob-feuer," a testing fire of purification</note> from which it arose in the beginning. The watchmen announce the dawn of the day. The fiery letters in the heart of Jesus Christ are stirred to the full pronouncement of the Word: *Arise, you who sleep! Arise, you dead, who were slain by the Antichristian dragon, the harlot, and the false prophet! Come here to the fiery judgment; come here to the eternal light, that you may sing there the Song of Moses and the Song of the Lamb, who has washed you from sins through his blood and led you out of the confused clamor of Babylon through his Word and Holy Gospel.*

9. Therefore, God-loving reader, in consideration of such devastation caused by the manifold "particular" and self-made theologies that still emerge and grow daily—indeed, under a high, cunning appearance and an angelic form—we must be extremely careful. We must test to whom we open our ears and to whom we entrust and grant our souls. For if we were to find ourselves seduced and deceived at last, the Word would judge us: *Behold, I have told you everything beforehand,* Mark 13:23. *Watch and pray; take heed; remain in me, so I will also remain in you. Whoever remains in me and I in him, he brings forth much fruit,* John 15:4, 5. *Do you not then recognize yourselves, that JESUS Christ is in you? Unless indeed you are disqualified,* <note>original: "untüchtig," meaning unfit, failing the test, or reprobate</note> 2 Cor. 13:5.

10. This shows us sufficiently that Christ himself is the <term>Theologus</term> <note>original Latin: "Theologus," the Divine Teacher or the one who speaks of God</note>, and his Word is the only <term>Theologia</term> <note>original Latin: "Theologia," the study or knowledge of God</note>, in which we should all remain and from which we should draw our highest satisfaction. Especially since God the Father has placed all treasures of wisdom and glory in Him, and has revealed and offered them through Him, according to his Word: *All that the Father has is mine,* John 16:15. *For you have given him power over all flesh, that he might give eternal life to all whom you have given him,* John 17:2.

11. Even though an unspeakable host of buyers and sellers within the so-called Christendom now continuously shout and write here and there, deafening all people, thereby [drowning out] the One, Holy, All-speaking Word—from which everything lives, and from which all songs of praise in time and eternity spring forth through men and angels—

# Postscript

<note>The text begins mid-sentence, continuing from the previous page's description of the spiritual state of the world.</note> ...is not heard nor recognized: yet God, in contrast, has sent his individual witness, John, as the voice calling for repentance. He is found not among the common people in Jerusalem, nor among the priests and scribes in the Temple, but in the wilderness by the Jordan. There he dwells alone in solitude and leads his individual voice toward repentance in the silence; for in silence, hearing is sharpened and born, whereas in the midst of much shouting, it is stifled and lost. He alone testifies against all the shouters and says: "It is not I, but the one who comes after me, who was before me." He points with his finger to the Lamb of God who bears the sin of the world—to the <term>Divine Teacher</term> <note>original: "Theologum"</note>, the Heavenly Instructor, who himself baptizes with the Holy Spirit by his own power. Then the heavens open, and the Father’s voice is heard: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; him you shall hear."

12. Therefore, we wish to bring this to the heart of the God-seeking reader: to look carefully at this present time, when everything stands in wretched confusion and mingling. For the most part, evil has gained the upper hand and the good is suppressed, cleared away as if into the wilderness, and ground into the dust. We say this so that the reader may know what he hears, reads, and accepts. However, since this choice is difficult to recognize and achieve through one's own ability and dim reason—especially where the heart is lukewarm and cold toward God—the Lord God sends here and there an "individual John." This is a messenger who speaks to humanity with a new, fiery tongue from the new birth in God—as from the essential, self-subsisting theology itself. Such a messenger first shatters their hearts through Divine power and thus prepares the way for Christ, the great Universal <term>Theologian</term> <note>original: "Theologo"</note> (who comes after him), who will then further baptize the soul with the Holy Spirit.

13. We wish to recommend such a man to the reader, according to the condition and necessity of this time—one whom the Lord God has provided and anointed with the spirit of godliness and deep understanding. This author is the late Doctor <term>Bartholomew Sclei</term> <note>Bartholomæus Sclei was a 16th-century writer associated with the mystical or "spiritualist" movements in Poland</note>, who lived toward the end of the last <term>century</term> <note>original: "Seculi"</note> in <term>Lesser Poland</term> <note>original: "Klein Pohlen," a historical region in the southern part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth</note>. We recommend that you read through this work diligently, but even more, that you press inward with prayerful meditation. Above all, we commend you to make it your own with a sighing heart toward God, who gave this light and who is its very essential power. In these pages, the reader will find what the rest of the world neither knows nor seeks: namely, 

1. What true **Theology** and the **Theologian** are: specifically, the universal **Word** of the Lord that creates, sustains, and sanctifies heaven and earth along with all creatures. 
2. What Nature and the Creature are: in which God has mirrored Himself according to the outflowing of His wisdom, in the name and character of His **Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyfaltigkeit"</note>; and thus He <term>presents</term> <note>original: "præsentiret"</note> Himself as an "All in All" in all things, filling all things with His omnipresence. 
3. What Man, His image, is: in whom God has concentrated and formed Himself according to eternity and time, together with all creatures. 
4. And finally, what Holy Scripture is. Namely, that it is also everything just mentioned: God in Christ, Nature, and Man. And all of this appears in a twofold form: for the good it leads to good, but for the evil it leads to evil—indeed, even becoming a snare and a misfortune—just as the author has richly and clearly set forth in these writings.

14. If you now see all of this with a seeing eye, then your heart will rejoice with us, who have recognized this in God, found it testified in the light of His grace, and concluded it with deep thanksgiving. Come, Lord Jesus Christ, you mighty God and Ruler, so that (Mark 4:36) the sea and the winds fall silent; so that (Matthew 9:23) the <term>pipers</term> <note>A reference to the professional mourners/flute players at the house of Jairus, representing worldly noise and mourning over spiritual death</note> and the tumult are driven out from before your face. Let your unique Word flourish in many; gather the scattered, wandering, and ransomed sparks of your breath and your outflowing Word, so that your name may be hallowed, and your song of praise alone may resound from everyone to the ends of the world, forever and ever.
